characters.name: Connie Rosolli

characters.description: Stephanie's former schoolmate and professional rival, now pursuing bounty work and ready to compete with Stephanie for Ranger's recovery.
characters.name: Joyce Barnhardt

characters.description: The dead member of the Ramos family whose murder and the burning of a building put Ranger under suspicion.
characters.name: Homer Ramos

characters.description: The powerful head of the Ramos family, whose wealth and influence are tied to a secretive weapons business. He wants Ranger found as urgently as the authorities do.
characters.name: Alexander Ramos

characters.description: A surviving member of the Ramos family involved in its business and its internal conflicts after Homer's death.
characters.name: Hannibal Ramos

characters.description: One of two men assigned to follow Stephanie in the hope that she will lead them to Ranger.
characters.name: Mitchell

characters.description: Mitchell's surveillance partner, also tasked with tracking Stephanie's contacts with Ranger.
characters.name: Habib

characters.description: A large, unruly dog who enters Stephanie and Morelli's lives and adds a domestic obligation neither planned for.
characters.name: Bob

recaps.ending: Stephanie's investigation establishes that Ranger did not murder Homer Ramos. Homer's death and the warehouse fire arose from conflict inside the Ramos family's illicit weapons business, and the surviving family's efforts to recover control created the surveillance and violence around Stephanie. The final confrontation exposes that internal betrayal and removes the basis for pursuing Ranger as the killer. Ranger remains outside ordinary expectations but is free of the homicide accusation. Repeated danger has pushed Stephanie into Morelli's house, where Grandma Mazur and Bob turn the arrangement into an improvised household. Morelli offers a recognizable shared life, while Ranger remains professionally indispensable and personally interested. Stephanie does not choose between them; Ranger instead leaves her with the understanding that the favors and protection exchanged between them carry a personal debt that will continue into the next case.
recaps.in_short: Ranger becomes a fugitive after Homer Ramos is murdered and a building burns, leaving evidence that points toward him. Vinnie asks Stephanie to recover his most capable agent, while police, rival bounty hunter Joyce Barnhardt, and men working for the wealthy Ramos family all follow the same trail. Ranger repeatedly contacts Stephanie but refuses custody, pushing her to investigate the family's hidden arms business and the conflict surrounding Homer's death. Lula helps in the field, and Morelli provides police knowledge while becoming increasingly protective. Threats to Stephanie's apartment, Grandma Mazur's temporary move, and the arrival of the dog Bob draw Stephanie into Morelli's home. The evidence finally clears Ranger and places the murder within the Ramos family's own criminal struggle. Ranger remains free, and the immediate case closes. Stephanie is left sharing domestic space with Morelli while owing Ranger for his intervention, preserving rather than resolving the attraction and rivalry among all three.

recaps.text: Previously: Stephanie Plum works as an apprehension agent for her cousin Vinnie, aided by office partner Lula and trained by the highly capable Ranger. Police officer Joe Morelli has moved from Stephanie's former lover and professional obstacle into a current but undefined relationship. In her last case, Stephanie found that her missing Uncle Fred had been murdered after encountering criminal activity connected to the refuse business. Ranger's secretive paid errands drew her closer to him, while Morelli remained the more familiar romantic partner. Stephanie ended that case without making a lasting choice between the two men.

Ranger is sought after Homer Ramos is found murdered and a building connected to the death is burned. Evidence places Ranger at the scene, and his disappearance turns him from Vinnie's best apprehension agent into a costly failure to appear. Vinnie assigns Stephanie to locate him even though both know Ranger can evade her whenever he chooses. Ranger makes contact on his own terms and denies being the killer, but refuses to surrender. Morelli approaches the matter as a police investigation and warns Stephanie that loyalty to Ranger does not make the evidence harmless. Joyce Barnhardt sees the open bond as a competing payday.

Stephanie follows the homicide into the Ramos family, whose wealth masks a dangerous weapons business and serious internal divisions. Alexander Ramos wants Ranger found, while Mitchell and Habib watch Stephanie in the expectation that Ranger will approach her. Their surveillance confirms that more than the police and the bond office are competing for him. Ranger continues to appear without allowing Stephanie to arrest him and directs her toward inconsistencies in the case. Lula assists with Stephanie's ordinary fugitive work, and Morelli supplies limited police information while objecting to the risks Stephanie accepts for Ranger.

The pressure around Stephanie expands from surveillance into direct danger. The warehouse, Homer's death, and the Ramos family's arms activity increasingly look like parts of a family conflict rather than a murder committed by an outside bounty hunter. Ranger's secrecy prevents Stephanie from proving that quickly, but his repeated opportunities to flee or silence her do not fit the official theory. Domestic disorder grows alongside the case: Grandma Mazur disrupts Stephanie's living arrangements, and Bob becomes an unexpected responsibility. Morelli's house begins to function as shelter as well as an expression of the relationship he wants Stephanie to take more seriously.

Stephanie and Morelli trace the evidence toward the struggle among the Ramos men and the illicit trade they are protecting. People following Stephanie are interested not simply in Ranger's arrest but in what he learned before the fire. Ranger remains close enough to intervene yet outside custody, forcing Stephanie to separate the case Vinnie assigned from the murder that must be solved before the bond problem can safely end. Attacks on Stephanie's home and routine push her further into Morelli's household. The arrangement offers security and intimacy, but it does not remove her attraction or obligation to Ranger.

The final confrontation exposes Homer's murder as part of the Ramos family's internal conflict over its illegal weapons business. The evidence that appeared to identify Ranger reflected his investigation and presence around the operation, not responsibility for the killing. With the guilty actors and their motives exposed, Ranger is cleared of the homicide accusation and no longer needs to remain a fugitive. Stephanie survives the violence surrounding the Ramos family and closes Vinnie's immediate bond crisis. She is now living in Morelli's house amid the disorder created by Grandma Mazur and Bob, but domestic proximity does not settle the relationship. Ranger remains her professional protector and romantic alternative, and the debt between them leaves that triangle active.

characters.description: A very old Irish Druid living under a modern identity in Tempe, Arizona, where he runs an occult bookshop and herb store. He draws power through bindings to the earth, can speak mind-to-mind with his hound, and carries the enchanted sword Fragarach. Centuries of evading hostile gods have made him resourceful, cautious, and fond of keeping several escape plans ready.
characters.name: Atticus O'Sullivan

characters.description: Atticus's enormous Irish wolfhound and constant companion. Their magical mental link lets him converse with Atticus in clear thoughts. He is loyal and brave, but his attention is easily captured by food, hunting, and the prospect of meeting other dogs.
characters.name: Oberon

characters.description: An Irish goddess associated with battle and death who has known Atticus for centuries. Formidable and unpredictable, she sometimes warns him of danger while making it clear that divine help always carries its own motives.
characters.name: The Morrigan

characters.description: The Irish god who has pursued Atticus across centuries for possessing Fragarach. Powerful, vindictive, and skilled at working through both supernatural agents and modern institutions, he is the threat Atticus has spent much of his long life avoiding.
characters.name: Aenghus Og

characters.description: Atticus's elderly Irish neighbor, a devout Catholic with a sharp eye for local activity and an unflappable acceptance of her unusual young friend. Their conversations give Atticus a welcome connection to ordinary human life.
characters.name: Mrs. MacDonagh

characters.description: A friendly bartender at Rula Bula who knows Atticus as a regular customer. Intelligent, curious, and more observant than he initially assumes, she is interested in the knowledge hidden behind his youthful appearance.
characters.name: Granuaile MacTiernan

characters.description: The leader of a Tempe coven whose members practice a Polish tradition of witchcraft. She approaches Atticus as a practical negotiator: her group can provide valuable magical help, but its history with him leaves ample reason for mutual caution.
characters.name: Malina Sokolowski

characters.description: The sovereign of the Irish Fae and a goddess of craft, healing, and poetry. She judges disputes involving her people with regal authority and expects old obligations and formal promises to be honored.
characters.name: Brighid

characters.description: A centuries-old vampire who employs Atticus's legal firm and conducts business with polished restraint. His knowledge of supernatural politics and willingness to exchange favors make him useful, though Atticus never forgets that a vampire's interests are not his own.
characters.name: Leif Helgarson

characters.description: A werewolf attorney at the firm that handles Atticus's legal affairs. Calm and exact in professional matters, he also serves as Atticus's link to the local pack and understands how readily supernatural trouble can become a police or courtroom problem.
characters.name: Hal Hauk

characters.description: An Irish goddess of wild animals and the hunt. Direct, dangerous, and far more comfortable in pursuit than in negotiation, she becomes involved when divine maneuvering brings a hunt to Atticus's territory.
characters.name: Flidais

characters.description: A formidable witch within Malina's coven whose ambitions and methods make her especially difficult for Atticus to read. Her presence complicates any alliance between the Druid and the witches.
characters.name: Radomila

recaps.ending: Atticus joins forces with the Morrigan, Flidais, and the Tempe witches for the confrontation Aenghus Og has forced upon him. The battle destroys Aenghus's remaining advantage, and Atticus kills the god who has hunted him for centuries, ending the immediate pursuit over Fragarach. The victory does not make Atticus safe: his alliances with gods, witches, vampires, and werewolves all involve debts that can be called in later. He returns to his life in Tempe with Oberon and keeps the sword. Granuaile, having learned that the supernatural world is real and that Atticus is a genuine Druid, asks him to teach her. He agrees to take her as his apprentice, beginning the long process of training a new Druid while trying to preserve the ordinary life and community he has built.
recaps.in_short: Atticus O'Sullivan, an ancient Irish Druid living as a young bookseller in Tempe, has spent centuries hiding from Aenghus Og, the god who wants both him and the enchanted sword Fragarach. When Aenghus finally moves against him, Atticus survives attacks by supernatural agents while also contending with police attention, old obligations among the Irish gods, and a wary local coven. His allies include his telepathic hound Oberon, the Morrigan, the hunt goddess Flidais, vampire lawyer Leif Helgarson, werewolf attorney Hal Hauk, and the witches led by Malina. Their interests overlap without ever becoming simple trust. Atticus ultimately turns Aenghus's schemes against him and kills the god, ending the pursuit that shaped much of his life. He remains in Tempe, still owing favors across the supernatural world, and agrees to train his friend Granuaile as a Druid.

recaps.text: Atticus O'Sullivan appears to be a young Tempe shopkeeper, but he is an Irish Druid more than two thousand years old. He draws magic from the earth, carries the enchanted sword Fragarach, and shares a mental bond with his Irish wolfhound, Oberon. Aenghus Og, an Irish god who has hunted him for centuries, has at last found him. The Morrigan warns Atticus that the threat is immediate. Atticus would prefer to keep the independent life he has built around his shop, his elderly neighbor Mrs. MacDonagh, and his friends at the pub, but attacks by Aenghus's agents make flight a poor solution. The conflict also draws attention from local police, forcing Atticus to defend himself without exposing what he is.

Atticus begins calling on the network he has built in Arizona. Malina Sokolowski's Polish witches offer information and magical assistance, although neither side forgets their uneasy history. His legal protection comes through Leif Helgarson, a vampire, and Hal Hauk, a werewolf attorney, tying his immediate problem to the local supernatural balance. Brighid, ruler of the Irish Fae, must also consider the competing claims and offenses surrounding Aenghus and Fragarach. Atticus learns that his enemy is using layers of agents, law, and old divine grievances so that defeating any single attacker will not settle the matter. He chooses to remain on ground where his bond to the earth is strongest and to prepare for a direct confrontation.

Further attacks confirm that Aenghus intends to isolate Atticus before closing in. Atticus uses iron, protective bindings, and his knowledge of different supernatural weaknesses to survive, while Oberon helps him track danger and escape ambushes. The Morrigan's warnings remain useful but never free of her own designs. Granuaile, the perceptive bartender Atticus knows from Rula Bula, sees enough of the upheaval to realize that his public identity conceals something extraordinary. As pressure grows, Atticus works to keep uninvolved friends out of the conflict and to prevent mortal authorities from interpreting supernatural violence as an ordinary crime with him at its center.

Flidais, goddess of the hunt, arrives as divine schemes bring a dangerous pursuit into Atticus's territory. Atticus survives by identifying where the gods' goals diverge rather than treating them as a united enemy. At the same time, dealings with Malina's coven grow more complicated, especially where the formidable Radomila is concerned. Atticus accepts that he cannot defeat Aenghus alone, but every prospective ally has a separate grievance or desired payment. He assembles a temporary coalition while continuing to use the Arizona earth as both refuge and source of strength. The approaching battle will decide whether he can finally stop running with Fragarach.

Atticus's alliances hold long enough for him to dismantle the traps surrounding Aenghus's attack. The witches contribute their own forms of magic, while Flidais and the Morrigan bring divine power that Atticus could not match directly. He uses Fragarach and his earth-based bindings with care, knowing that a mistake could cut him off from the source of his strength. Aenghus is forced out from behind intermediaries and into the conflict himself. The old pursuit has become a final contest, but Atticus also recognizes that success will leave him owing favors to allies whose future requests may be nearly as dangerous as his present enemy.

In the final confrontation, Atticus and his temporary allies overcome Aenghus Og's forces, and Atticus kills the god who has hunted him for centuries. He retains Fragarach and returns to Tempe alive, but the network of bargains that made the victory possible remains in place. Leif, Hal, the witches, and the Irish gods all know that Atticus can be drawn into supernatural affairs, and some have favors still to collect. Granuaile now understands that Atticus is an ancient Druid rather than an unusually knowledgeable bookseller. She asks to learn his tradition, and Atticus accepts her as his apprentice. With Oberon beside him, he resumes his Arizona life free of Aenghus's pursuit but tied to a new responsibility and several unresolved debts.

characters.description: A twenty-three-year-old half-human, half-Fae woman living in Crescent City, where she works as an assistant at Griffin Antiquities, a gallery dealing in rare and dangerous artifacts. Sharp-tongued, sociable, and devoted to her small circle of friends, she spends her nights in the city's clubs and her days cataloguing objects most people never see. Her Fae father never claimed her; she was raised by her human mother, Ember, and her human stepfather, Randall, and she uses her mother's name deliberately. Beyond Fae speed and quick healing she has no magic worth speaking of, and full-blooded Fae are quick to remind her of it.
characters.name: Bryce Quinlan

characters.description: Alpha of the Pack of Devils and heir to the Prime of the wolf shifters, and Bryce's closest friend and roommate. Reckless, funny, and fiercely protective, she leads her pack through the Aux, the city's civilian auxiliary force, and takes private security work on the side. In the weeks before the book opens she has been strained and secretive about a job she will not discuss, and she talks Bryce into having a long line of old Fae script tattooed down her spine.
characters.name: Danika Fendyr

characters.description: Danika's Second in the Pack of Devils, a wolf shifter who has been openly and patiently interested in Bryce for years. Steadier than the rest of the pack, he finally persuades her to agree to a real date rather than another night out with the group.
characters.name: Connor Holstrom

characters.description: A sorceress and Bryce's employer, owner of Griffin Antiquities, where she trades in artifacts and books too dangerous for open sale. Once a witch, she now belongs to the House of Flame and Shadow, and she is rumored to turn people who displease her into animals. She is exacting, unsentimental, and rarely explains herself.
characters.name: Jesiba Roga

characters.description: A malakh, or angel, known across Midgard as the Umbra Mortis. Two centuries ago he fought in a failed rebellion against the Archangels and was captured; since then he has been enslaved, his brow marked with the halo tattoo that binds most of his power and his forearm bearing the mark of whichever Archangel currently owns him. He works off an enormous debt of assassinations for Micah Domitus, Governor of Valbara, and is offered a chance at freedom if he can find the killer Bryce is hunting. Grim, exhausted, and slow to trust, he is assigned to her as much to watch her as to work with her.
characters.name: Hunt Athalar

characters.description: The Archangel who governs Valbara from the Comitium towers in Crescent City, answerable only to the Asteri who rule Midgard. Immaculate, unhurried, and absolute, he owns Hunt Athalar outright and treats the city's other leaders as subordinates. He takes a personal interest in the killings and puts Bryce and Hunt on them together.
characters.name: Micah Domitus

characters.description: A fire sprite the size of a doll who lives in the climate-controlled library beneath Griffin Antiquities, where she minds the collection and keeps Bryce company. She is indentured to Jesiba, watches soap operas obsessively, and is romantic, talkative, and frightened of nearly everything outside her library.
characters.name: Lehabah

characters.description: Crown Prince of the Valbaran Fae and Bryce's half-brother, son of the Autumn King. He keeps company with two Fae lords' sons, wears his hair long enough to irritate his father, and bears Gwydion, the Starsword, an ancient blade of the Starborn line that only he can wield. His gift is mind-to-mind speech. He and Bryce have been estranged for years after a confrontation neither has forgiven, and the murders push him back into her life.
characters.name: Ruhn Danaan

characters.description: Danika's mother and Prime Apparent of the wolf shifters, waiting to inherit leadership from her aged father. Cold and openly contemptuous of Bryce, she blames her for her daughter's death and has spent two years making that clear.
characters.name: Sabine Fendyr

characters.description: Commander of the 33rd Imperial Legion in Crescent City and, like Hunt, a survivor of the failed angelic rebellion who has spent two centuries in an Archangel's service. Polished and diplomatic where Hunt is blunt, he is Hunt's oldest friend and the one holding their unit together.
characters.name: Isaiah Tiberian

characters.description: Connor's younger brother, a wolf shifter and a star player on a university sunball team. He and Bryce were close before the massacre took his brother and the rest of the pack, and the loss has left the two of them unable to face each other.
characters.name: Ithan Holstrom

characters.description: The Fae King of Valbara, Ruhn's father and Bryce's biological father, who has never publicly acknowledged her. Ancient, precise, and interested in his children mainly as instruments, he keeps a private laboratory and a very long memory, and he wants to know exactly what Bryce has been asked to investigate.
characters.name: The Autumn King

characters.description: A human assassin for hire and one of the friends Bryce ran with before Danika's death, with a reputation on two continents and a habit of appearing without warning. She has resources and contacts the investigation badly needs, and a long, complicated history with Bryce's other friends.
characters.name: Fury Axtar

characters.description: A faun and a principal dancer with Crescent City's ballet company, another of Bryce's old circle. Warm and disciplined where Bryce is chaotic, she was hurt by Bryce's withdrawal after the murders.
characters.name: Juniper Andromeda

characters.description: A mer male who serves as Captain of Intelligence for the River Queen, whose court lies beneath the Istros. Easygoing and quick with a joke, he handles anything that surfaces in the river, which makes him useful to Bryce and Hunt as bodies begin turning up.
characters.name: Tharion Ketos

characters.description: The newly crowned Witch-Queen of Valbara, young and quiet, recently succeeded to a throne her mother held for centuries. Trained as a healer, she keeps to herself among the region's louder leaders and is watched closely by those who expected an easier queen.
characters.name: Hypaxia Enador

characters.description: One of the seven Princes of Hel, master of the Chasm, who spoke to Bryce once when she was a small child and has taken an unexplained interest in her since. He is courteous, amused, and unwilling to say plainly what he wants from her.
characters.name: Aidas

characters.description: Archangel and Governor of a swathe of Pangera, and the twin sister of Shahar, the Archangel Hunt loved and followed into rebellion. She is notorious for what she does to those she owns, keeps the empire's cruelest soldiers in her personal guard, and arrives in Crescent City for the Summit with an obvious interest in acquiring the Umbra Mortis.
characters.name: Sandriel

recaps.ending: Micah Domitus is exposed as the murderer of Danika Fendyr and her pack, killed for stealing the Horn of Luna, and as the architect of the killings staged since to force the artifact into the open. He opens a rift above Crescent City so that he can be the one to close it, and demons overrun the streets. Lehabah dies saving Bryce and Hunt from the kristallos in the gallery library, and Hunt's wings are destroyed in the fighting. Micah is killed. Bryce, having realized that Danika hid the Horn by grinding it into the ink of her tattoo, runs the city's ancient Gates and channels Hunt's lightning through the Horn in her skin, waking Starborn light nobody knew she carried. She seals the rift, drives the demons back, and heals much of the damage, nearly dying in the process. Afterward she makes the Drop into her full immortal power with Hunt as her Anchor and survives it. Hunt's two centuries of enslavement end and he stays in Crescent City with her. Bryce is publicly acknowledged as Starborn and as a Fae princess she never wanted to be, watched now by her father the Autumn King, by the Asteri, and by the Princes of Hel, and she is still carrying the Horn. The empire's war against the human rebels of Pangera continues untouched.
recaps.in_short: In Crescent City on the world of Midgard, half-human, half-Fae Bryce Quinlan comes home one night to find her best friend, the wolf Alpha Danika Fendyr, and Danika's entire pack slaughtered, apparently by a demon. Two years later the killings resume, clearing the human rebel convicted of them, and the Archangel who governs the city orders Bryce to investigate alongside Hunt Athalar, an enslaved fallen angel promised his freedom if he finds the killer. Their search leads through a synthetic drug trade, a demon bred to hunt by scent, and the theft of the Horn of Luna, a broken Fae artifact that can open passages between worlds. The killer proves to be the Archangel himself, who murdered Danika for stealing the Horn and staged the later deaths to force it into the open. Bryce discovers that Danika hid the Horn by grinding it into the ink of Bryce's own tattoo. When the Archangel opens a rift and demons flood the city, Bryce wakes the Horn with Hunt's lightning, reveals herself as Starborn, and seals the rift. The Archangel dies, Hunt is freed, and Bryce comes into her full power.

recaps.text: Crescent City, also called Lunathion, is the largest city of Valbara on the world of Midgard, where immortal Vanir rule and humans live as a subject caste under the distant authority of the Asteri. Bryce Quinlan, twenty-three and half human, half Fae, works at Griffin Antiquities for the sorceress Jesiba Roga and shares an apartment with her closest friend, Danika Fendyr, Alpha of the Pack of Devils and heir to the wolves' leadership. Their nights are spent in the city's clubs with Danika's pack, including her Second, Connor Holstrom, who finally persuades Bryce to agree to a proper date. Danika has been tense and evasive about private security work she refuses to describe, and she talks Bryce into having a line of old Fae script inked down her spine. Danika's pack has recently arrested Philip Briggs, a human rebel accused of plotting to bomb a club, and he is released on a technicality. After a night out and a strange, hurried message from Danika, Bryce comes home to find Danika and the entire Pack of Devils torn apart in the apartment, apparently by a demon. Briggs is arrested for the killings, and Bryce is left alive and alone.

Two years later, Bryce is still at the gallery and still living with what she found in that apartment, holding her old friends at arm's length. Then a vampyr is killed in the city with the same signature as the massacre, something Philip Briggs, locked up ever since, could not have done. Micah Domitus, the Archangel who governs Valbara, orders Bryce to assist the investigation, since she knew the first victims better than anyone. He assigns her Hunt Athalar, the angel called the Umbra Mortis, a survivor of a failed rebellion against the Archangels who has been enslaved for two centuries and works off a debt of assassinations for whoever owns him. Micah offers Hunt an end to that debt if the killer is found. Neither of them wants the arrangement: he expects a spoiled party girl, she expects a minder. They begin retracing Danika's last days and the trail of a killer who has been quiet for two years.

The evidence points away from a human bomber and toward something summoned. The weapon is a kristallos, a hybrid demon whose venom the medwitches can identify, and a demon of that kind has to be called through by a powerful Vanir, which narrows the field to the city's leadership. The investigation drags Bryce back into Fae politics and toward her half-brother, Ruhn Danaan, Crown Prince of the Valbaran Fae, who carries the ancient Starsword and can speak mind to mind. Their father, the Autumn King, has never acknowledged Bryce publicly and takes an interest in the case for reasons of his own. Working together, Bryce and Hunt begin to take each other's measure: she learns what the halo on his brow costs him, and he learns that her flippancy is armor over two years of grief.

The trail runs down into the city's underside. In the Meat Market, a walled bazaar run by the Viper Queen, Bryce and Hunt find traces of synth, a synthetic drug that gives a user brief, violent power and burns out the body that takes it. Danika had been working private security for Redner Industries in her last months and had learned something she never passed on to Bryce. Bodies keep surfacing in the Istros, which draws in Tharion Ketos, Captain of Intelligence for the River Queen's court beneath the river. Slowly a second motive emerges behind the killings: whoever is directing the demon appears to be searching the city for an object rather than for a person, and the object is the Horn of Luna, a broken Fae artifact once able to open passages between worlds.

Attacks come closer to Bryce herself, and she and Hunt are nearly killed more than once. Her mother, Ember, and her stepfather, Randall, make plain how far they will go to keep her out of Vanir hands, and Bryce refuses to leave the city. Hunt tells her about Shahar, the Archangel who led the Fallen against the Asteri's order and died at the end of that rebellion, and about the two centuries he has spent being sold from one Archangel to the next since. The partnership shifts into something closer to trust. Meanwhile the picture of Danika's last weeks keeps darkening: her behaviour was not that of a bodyguard doing routine work, and Bryce has to accept that her best friend was keeping something enormous from her.

Chasing what Danika knew, Bryce and Hunt cross the Istros to the Bone Quarter, the walled necropolis where the city's dead are ferried and where the Under-King rules, and come away with more questions than answers about where Danika's soul went. Ruhn works his own sources among the Fae, including a visit to the Oracle. Fury Axtar, the assassin, and Juniper Andromeda, the dancer, come back into Bryce's life after two years of silence, and the old circle reassembles around the case. The pieces finally resolve into one conclusion: before she died, Danika stole the Horn of Luna and hid it somewhere nobody has been able to find, and that theft is why she and her entire pack were killed.

With the Horn established as the prize, everyone's interest in Bryce becomes clearer and more dangerous. Sabine Fendyr, Danika's mother and heir to the wolves' leadership, is openly hostile and a plausible suspect. The Autumn King wants the Horn for the Fae. Micah keeps a tight grip on both the investigation and on Hunt, and reminds Hunt regularly of what his freedom is worth. Bryce learns that Danika had been taking synth herself, another secret kept from her, and has to reconcile the friend she remembers with the one the evidence describes. Whatever is between her and Hunt stops being deniable, and both of them understand what it will cost him if Micah decides to notice.

The leaders of Valbara gather for the Summit: Micah, the Autumn King, Sabine, the newly crowned Witch-Queen Hypaxia Enador, and, from the war-torn continent of Pangera, the Archangel Sandriel, twin sister of the Shahar whom Hunt loved and followed into rebellion. Sandriel's reputation for what she does to those she owns arrives ahead of her, and her interest in acquiring the Umbra Mortis is immediate. Bryce uses the gathering to press the case in public and makes enemies doing it. Another attack makes it undeniable that the killer is one of the people in the room. By the end of the Summit, arrangements are under way to hand Hunt over to Sandriel, and the freedom he was promised is gone.

Hunt is transferred to Sandriel and taken into her household, where she makes plain what the rest of his existence will look like under her and her guard, chief among them Pollux Antonius, the Hammer. Rather than accept it, Hunt kills her, an act no enslaved angel is expected to survive. Bryce, cut off from him, keeps working the case alone and closes the last distance to the truth about Danika's final days: what she stole, why she hid it, and who wanted it badly enough to slaughter a pack of wolves in their own home.

The killer is Micah Domitus. He tore Danika and the Pack of Devils apart himself after she stole the Horn and refused to hand it over, disguising the murders as a demon attack, and he bred the kristallos precisely because it can scent the Horn. Every killing since was staged to flush the artifact into the open and to keep the investigation pointed anywhere but at him, and putting Bryce and Hunt on the case was itself part of the search. With the truth out he stops pretending: Hunt is shackled and beaten for killing Sandriel, and Micah turns his full attention to finding what Danika hid.

Bryce finally understands where the Horn has been for two years. Danika ground it to dust and mixed it into the ink of the tattoo she talked Bryce into having put down her back; Bryce has been carrying it the whole time. In the gallery the kristallos corners them, and Lehabah, the fire sprite of the library, burns herself out to save Bryce and Hunt. Micah takes Bryce, and once he has what he wants he opens a rift above Crescent City and lets Hel's demons pour through, intending to be seen closing it again. Hunt's wings are destroyed. Bryce swallows synth to stay on her feet, and in the fighting that follows Micah is killed. With the city overrun, Bryce runs its ancient Gates, paying each one in blood, and uses Hunt's lightning to wake the Horn buried in her skin. What answers is Starborn light, the mark of the oldest Fae line, and with it she seals the rift, turns the demons back, and heals what she can of the city. In the aftermath she makes the Drop into her full power with Hunt as her Anchor and comes back alive. Hunt's enslavement ends, and the two of them are left together in a city that now knows exactly what Bryce Quinlan is.

characters.description: Stranded in a world she had never heard of, carrying the Starsword and the Horn of Luna inked into her back, with everyone she loves either captured or hunted on Midgard. She is the Starborn heir and a Fae princess by an accident of birth she never wanted, and where she has landed none of that means anything to anyone.
characters.name: Bryce Quinlan

characters.description: Taken alive by the Asteri and imprisoned beneath the Eternal City with a fresh set of restraints and no illusions about what is coming. He has been enslaved before and knows exactly how this goes; what he does not know is whether Bryce survived going through the portal.
characters.name: Hunt Athalar

characters.description: Crown Prince of the Valbaran Fae and Bryce's half-brother, captured with Hunt and held in the Asteri's cells. His mind-to-mind link with the rebel agent who calls herself Daybright is the one thing left to him that his captors cannot see or take.
characters.name: Ruhn Danaan

characters.description: The Hind, the Asteri's spymaster and interrogator, given charge of the prisoners taken in Crescent City. She has destroyed rebel cells across two continents, and every prisoner she has ever handled has broken.
characters.name: Lidia Cervos

characters.description: The Hammer, the imperial guard's most notorious soldier, who has waited a long time for Hunt Athalar to be handed to him with nobody left to intervene.
characters.name: Pollux Antonius

characters.description: The angel called the Helhound, imprisoned alongside Hunt and Ruhn. He was Danika Fendyr's mate, and of the three of them he is the one with least left to lose.
characters.name: Baxian Argos

characters.description: A wolf shifter with no pack, left in an occupied Crescent City carrying the knowledge of what the Bone Quarter actually does to the dead. Grieving, guilty and short of anyone to answer to, he keeps returning to the Astronomer and the mystics kept in tanks beneath his shop, and he is not thinking especially clearly about any of it.
characters.name: Ithan Holstrom

characters.description: Formerly Captain of Intelligence for the River Queen, now indentured to the Viper Queen and fighting in her pits. Escaping one owner has cost him considerably more than he expected.
characters.name: Tharion Ketos

characters.description: A warrior of the Night Court in the world of Prythian, carrying a power drawn from a Cauldron and a sword she did not ask for. She is among the first to confront Bryce after a stranger falls out of a portal into the middle of her home.
characters.name: Nesta Archeron

characters.description: Spymaster of Prythian's Night Court, a shadowsinger who carries a dagger called Truth-Teller. Quiet and watchful, he is the first to grasp that the newcomer's sword and his own blade were made as a matched pair, and therefore that the two worlds share a history nobody has recorded.
characters.name: Azriel

characters.description: High Lord of the Night Court in Prythian, who has to decide what to do about a stranger who arrived through a hole in the world carrying artifacts his own people have a history with, and how much of his court's business to tell her.
characters.name: Rhysand

characters.description: The Bright Hand of the Asteri, spokesman for the immortal parasites who have farmed Midgard for fifteen thousand years. Patient and unfailingly courteous, he treats the suppression of a rebellion as an accounting exercise.
characters.name: Rigelus

characters.description: The Witch-Queen of Valbara, whose training in necromancy has been a secret her entire life. With the Governor's court compromised and the city under imperial control, she is one of the few powers left in Lunathion still willing to act.
characters.name: Hypaxia Enador

characters.description: A wolf shifter kept among the Astronomer's mystics, the last true heir of the Fendyr line, held in a tank and used as a living instrument since she was a child. She has never known anything outside it.
characters.name: Sigrid Fendyr

characters.description: A Fae noblewoman of Valbara and Tristan Flynn's sister, whose family intends to marry her to a match she refuses. Composed, immaculately raised, and a great deal harder to intimidate than she appears.
characters.name: Sathia Flynn

characters.description: Prince of the Chasm and one of the seven Princes of Hel, who has watched Bryce since she was a small child. His interest in her ancestor Theia is very old and not entirely a matter of politics.
characters.name: Aidas

characters.description: Prince of the Pit and the most powerful of the Princes of Hel, called the Star-Eater. He fought the Asteri once before and lost, and he regards Bryce's bloodline as his own concern.
characters.name: Apollion

characters.description: A daughter of Theia, the Starborn queen who brought the Fae to Midgard, who left behind a record of what actually happened beneath the Fae island of Avallen for whoever eventually came looking for it.
characters.name: Silene

recaps.ending: Bryce lets the Asteri take her in order to reach the crystal at the heart of the Eternal City, where fifteen thousand years of power harvested from Midgard is stored. Her allies converge on the city from three directions: the fugitives Lidia Cervos broke out of the Asteri's cells, the wolves, mer, witches and Fae of Valbara, and the Princes of Hel, whose war against the Asteri long predates Midgard. Lidia settles her account with Pollux. Apollion takes his revenge on the Asteri in person. Bryce brings the Starsword and Truth-Teller together and uses them with the Horn of Luna to break the Asteri's hold on the world's power at its source. Rigelus is killed and the Asteri are destroyed. The cost is severe and several of those closest to Bryce come very near death. Midgard is left free and broken at once: the firstlight system that ran every city was the parasites' machinery, the Bone Quarter's consumption of the dead is finished, and there is no imperial government left standing. Bryce refuses the rule she is offered and leaves the shape of the new world to the people living in it, with humans no longer a subject caste. Hunt survives and stays with her, out from under the Asteri's ownership for good. Ruhn and Lidia are together and her sons are safe. Tharion, Ithan, Hypaxia, Baxian and the rest survive, several of them permanently altered by what it took. Hel stands as an ally rather than a threat, and the link between Midgard and Prythian, with the shared history it exposed, is now known in both worlds.
recaps.in_short: Stranded in Prythian after escaping Crescent City through a portal, Bryce Quinlan bargains with the Night Court for a way home and learns that the Starsword's twin, a dagger called Truth-Teller, has been in that world all along, evidence that Midgard's Fae arrived from Prythian as refugees. She returns carrying Truth-Teller and the Mask, an artifact that commands the dead. Meanwhile Hunt Athalar, Ruhn Danaan and Baxian Argos are tortured in the Asteri's cells until Lidia Cervos, the Hind, reveals herself as Daybright, the rebellion's long-hidden source inside the empire, and breaks them out. On Avallen the group finds a record left by Theia's daughter Silene showing how the Fae let the Asteri into Midgard and how everything the Fae have said about themselves since has been a fabrication. With Ophion destroyed and the empire in control, Bryce allows herself to be taken to the Eternal City in order to reach the crystal storing the power harvested from the world. In the battle that follows the Princes of Hel join the fight, Lidia kills Pollux, and Bryce uses the reunited blades and the Horn to break the Asteri's hold. The Asteri are destroyed, Midgard is freed, and the survivors are left to rebuild a world with no empire and no harvest.

recaps.text:
Previously, in the Crescent City books: on Midgard, a world ruled by the Asteri from the Eternal City, Bryce Quinlan discovered that the Archangel Micah had murdered her best friend Danika Fendyr and Danika's entire wolf pack in order to recover the Horn of Luna, a broken Fae artifact that can open passages between worlds. Danika had hidden the Horn by grinding it into the ink of Bryce's tattoo. When Micah opened a rift above Crescent City, Bryce woke the Horn with the lightning of Hunt Athalar, an enslaved fallen angel, sealed the rift, and revealed herself as Starborn. Micah died, Hunt was freed, and Bryce made the Drop into her full power.

Six months later the Fae prince Cormac Donnall, betrothed to Bryce against both their wishes, revealed himself as an agent of the human rebel network Ophion and drew Bryce, Hunt, her half-brother Ruhn Danaan, the mer Tharion Ketos and the exiled wolf Ithan Holstrom into a search for a missing boy. What they found instead was the truth about their world: the Asteri are parasites who arrived fifteen thousand years ago, the firstlight powering every city is harvested from the Vanir themselves, and the souls ferried to the Bone Quarter are consumed rather than laid to rest. It was what Danika had died knowing. Rigelus, the Bright Hand of the Asteri, then came for Bryce and the Horn. Cormac was killed. Hunt, Ruhn and the angel Baxian Argos were captured alive and shipped to the Eternal City to be broken by the Hind, the empire's spymaster, and Pollux the Hammer. Cornered at one of Crescent City's Gates, Bryce channeled Hunt's lightning through the Horn and tore open a portal out of the world, stepping through with the Starsword. She landed in Prythian, a world she had never heard of, and was met by a winged male trailing shadows and a woman holding a dagger that is the Starsword's twin. Ruhn's anonymous rebel contact, Daybright, remains unidentified. Tharion has sold his service to the Viper Queen to escape the River Queen. Midgard is under the Asteri's control, and nobody who could act on the truth is free to do so.

Bryce arrives in Prythian with no way home and is taken in hand by the Night Court, who treat her as a threat until she gives them reason not to. She meets Nesta Archeron and the shadowsinger Azriel, whose dagger Truth-Teller matches the Starsword exactly, and it becomes clear the two blades were made as a pair by the same hand. Bryce trades what she knows about Midgard for help getting back, and starts assembling the history of how the Fae reached her world at all. On Midgard, Hunt, Ruhn and Baxian are held in the Asteri's cells beneath the Eternal City, worked over by Pollux under the Hind's supervision, while she conducts her interrogations with the same efficiency she has applied to every rebel she has ever taken.

In the cells, Ruhn discovers that Daybright, the anonymous rebel who has been feeding Ophion the empire's secrets for years, is Lidia Cervos herself, and that the Hind has been running both sides for far longer than anyone guessed. Her position depends entirely on nobody knowing, and her two sons are held elsewhere as a guarantee of her loyalty. In Crescent City, Ithan Holstrom pursues the Astronomer's mystics and confirms that one of them is Sigrid Fendyr, a true wolf heir raised in a tank. Tharion, indentured to the Viper Queen, fights in her pits and looks for a way out that does not cost him more than the last one did. Bryce, still in Prythian, bargains for the means to reopen a portal home.

Bryce returns to Midgard carrying more than she left with: Truth-Teller, the Starsword's twin, and the Mask, an artifact from the same ancient set as the Horn, which gives its wearer command over the dead. Lidia gives up her cover to break Hunt, Ruhn and Baxian out of the Asteri's prison, an escape that destroys everything she has spent years building and puts her sons in immediate danger. Ithan frees Sigrid from the Astronomer's tank, and it goes catastrophically wrong: a wolf raised in isolation and starved of everything is not the heir he had imagined, and both of them pay for his decision.

The survivors scatter and regroup. Hunt, Ruhn, Baxian and Lidia are fugitives with the whole imperial apparatus hunting them, and the alliance between them is uneasy: Ruhn has to reconcile the voice he trusted for years with the woman who tortured his friends, and Hunt has no interest in forgiving her at all. Bryce, back on Midgard and hunted hardest of any of them, works to reach the others. Crescent City is under occupation, Ophion has been destroyed as a fighting force, and the question is no longer how to win the war but whether an Asteri can be killed at all.

Answers come from two directions. The Princes of Hel, Apollion and Aidas, make plain that their war has always been against the Asteri and that Bryce's bloodline is why they keep intervening in Midgard's affairs. And on Avallen, the Fae island of mists, Bryce and Ruhn find a record left by Silene, a daughter of Theia, the Starborn queen who led the Fae to Midgard. It shows what actually happened: the Fae did not arrive as conquerors bringing civilization but as refugees fleeing another world, and it was they who let the Asteri in. The version of history the Fae have told for fifteen thousand years is a fabrication built over that. The Horn, the Mask and the twin blades all turn out to be pieces of the same original set.

With the true history in hand, the group works out what the Asteri actually are and where they can be reached. Everything in the Eternal City runs through a single vast crystal that stores the power harvested from Midgard, and the Asteri themselves are not indestructible. Freeing Lidia's sons, held by an Archangel loyal to the empire, becomes the first objective. Tharion cuts himself loose from the Viper Queen at a price, and a marriage of convenience to Sathia Flynn buys him a footing back in Valbara. Hypaxia Enador, whose necromancy has been a lifelong secret, stops hiding it and commits herself openly to the fight.

The pieces move toward the Eternal City. Lidia's sons are recovered, at cost, and she stops pretending she is anything other than fully committed; she and Ruhn stop pretending about each other as well. The Asteri prepare for what they know is coming and turn Midgard's own defenses toward it, while Rigelus works on a solution of his own to the problem Bryce represents. Ithan, changed beyond recovery by what happened with Sigrid, is no longer simply a wolf. Bryce concludes that the only way to reach the Asteri is to let them take her.

Bryce goes to the Eternal City and into Rigelus's hands, gambling that proximity is worth what it will cost her. What the Asteri want is the Horn and the Starborn power that can wake it, and Rigelus intends to use both to open a lasting passage and secure the empire against anything Hel can send through. Bryce sees the crystal at the heart of the palace and understands what fifteen thousand years of harvest looks like when it is stored in one place. Her allies converge on the city from several directions, and the rest of Midgard's powers are forced to choose a side in the open.

The attack on the Eternal City begins. The imperial legions, the Asteri's constructs and the empire's Archangels are thrown against a coalition that should never have existed: fugitive rebels, wolves, mer, witches, Fae and the Princes of Hel. Hunt's lightning and Bryce's Starborn light together prove to be the only combination that can touch an Asteri directly. Lidia settles her account with Pollux. Losses on both sides are severe, and several of the Asteri are killed, which nobody on Midgard believed possible.

Rigelus makes his last moves, and the fighting turns on control of the crystal and the harvested power stored inside it. Apollion, who lost this war once already, takes his revenge on the Asteri in person. Bryce brings the Starsword and Truth-Teller together and uses them with the Horn to break the Asteri's grip on Midgard's power at its source. The cost is heavy, those closest to her come near death, and the systems that have run the world on harvested firstlight for fifteen thousand years begin to fail as the hold on them breaks.

The Asteri are destroyed and the harvesting of Midgard ends. Rigelus is killed, and with the parasites gone the world has to be rebuilt from the ground up: the firstlight grid that powered every city was the Asteri's machinery, the Bone Quarter's traffic in souls is finished, and Hel becomes an ally rather than the threat the empire always claimed. Bryce survives, changed by what she channeled, and refuses the rule she is offered; what Midgard becomes is left to be argued out by the people who live there, humans included, rather than dictated from the Eternal City. Hunt survives and stays with her, out from under the Asteri's ownership for good. Ruhn and Lidia, who spent the war lying to each other by necessity, are together, and her sons are safe. Tharion, Ithan, Hypaxia, Baxian and the rest of the circle survive, several of them permanently altered by what it took to get here. The passage to Prythian, and the shared history it exposed, is now a known fact in both worlds rather than a secret buried under an island.

characters.description: Half human and half Fae, and now publicly known as Starborn after the battle that saved Crescent City. She still works at Griffin Antiquities, still carries the Horn of Luna in the ink down her back, and is living with Hunt Athalar. The title she never wanted has bought her a seat at Fae tables she despises and the steady attention of everyone who would like to know what she can actually do.
characters.name: Bryce Quinlan

characters.description: The angel once called the Umbra Mortis, free for the first time in two centuries although the halo tattoo remains on his brow. He flies with the 33rd under Isaiah Tiberian, lives with Bryce, and is credited across Midgard with the deaths of two Archangels, something the Asteri have not forgotten. He wants an ordinary life and does not expect to be allowed one.
characters.name: Hunt Athalar

characters.description: Crown Prince of the Valbaran Fae and Bryce's half-brother, bearer of the Starsword. Since the events of the previous book he has been pulled into the orbit of the human rebellion, taking instructions mind to mind from an anonymous agent who uses the code name Daybright and whose real identity he is forbidden to try to learn.
characters.name: Ruhn Danaan

characters.description: A wolf shifter with no pack, living on Bryce and Hunt's couch after being cast out by the wolves. He has lost the place he was raised for and is quietly consumed by the question of what became of his brother Connor's soul after the massacre.
characters.name: Ithan Holstrom

characters.description: Captain of Intelligence for the River Queen, whose court lies beneath the Istros. Charming and evasive, he serves a monarch who does not accept refusals, and he is sent to find a missing human boy before anyone else can.
characters.name: Tharion Ketos

characters.description: A young human working for Ophion, the network fighting the Asteri's empire, and a thunderbird: a rare wielder of lightning that the empire hunts on sight. She is taken by imperial forces after infiltrating a labor camp to reach her younger brother.
characters.name: Sofie Renast

characters.description: Known across Midgard as the Hind, a deer shifter who serves the Asteri as spymaster and chief interrogator. She has broken more rebel cells than anyone alive, travels with the empire's worst soldiers, and her name is a byword for how far the empire's reach extends.
characters.name: Lidia Cervos

characters.description: An angel of the imperial guard called the Hammer, the most notorious soldier in the Asteri's service. After Sandriel's death he attached himself to the Hind, and he has a long record of atrocities carried out on the empire's behalf.
characters.name: Pollux Antonius

characters.description: The Archangel newly installed as Governor of Valbara in Micah's place. Mild, conciliatory, and apparently uninterested in cruelty, she arrives intending to run the territory differently from her predecessor, and comes with orders from the Asteri concerning her own marriage.
characters.name: Celestina

characters.description: Prince of Avallen, the mist-shrouded Fae island across the sea, and a warrior whose gift is teleporting. Bryce's father betroths her to him without her consent, an arrangement neither of them wants. Grieving and single-minded, he has his own reasons for coming to Crescent City.
characters.name: Cormac Donnall

characters.description: Sofie's younger brother, a human boy held for years in an imperial labor camp and missing since his sister's capture. Ophion, the empire, and half the powers of Crescent City are all looking for him, each convinced he is worth a great deal.
characters.name: Emile Renast

characters.description: An angel called the Helhound, formerly of Sandriel's guard and now posted to Crescent City's legion. He tracks by scent, keeps his own counsel, and shadows Bryce and Hunt more closely than his duties account for.
characters.name: Baxian Argos

characters.description: The young Witch-Queen of Valbara, a trained healer who has been quietly working as a medwitch in the city. The Asteri have arranged her marriage to the new Governor, and she accepts it with the composure of someone long accustomed to having her life decided for her.
characters.name: Hypaxia Enador

characters.description: A human assassin and one of Bryce's oldest friends, with contacts on both sides of the war and a policy of explaining nothing. She works for clients Bryce has learned not to ask about.
characters.name: Fury Axtar

characters.description: The Bright Hand of the Asteri, spokesman for the immortal rulers who govern Midgard from the Eternal City. He wears the body of an adolescent boy, speaks with unhurried courtesy, and treats the affairs of an entire world as a long-running arithmetic problem.
characters.name: Rigelus

characters.description: Commander of Ophion's Lightfall squadron, a human rebel officer who regards Vanir of every kind as targets to be eliminated. Her methods unsettle her own side as much as the enemy.
characters.name: Pippa Spetsos

characters.description: The ruler of the Meat Market, a shifter who deals in fights, drugs and information and honors a contract precisely as written. Very little moves through the city's underside without her knowledge.
characters.name: The Viper Queen

characters.description: One of the seven Princes of Hel, master of the Chasm, who has known Bryce since she was a child. He appears when he chooses, answers only the questions that suit him, and clearly wants something from her bloodline.
characters.name: Aidas

recaps.ending: Rigelus and the Asteri move openly against Crescent City once Bryce is identified as the Starborn heir carrying the Horn of Luna. Cormac Donnall is killed in the fighting, and the rebellion in Valbara is dismantled. Hunt Athalar, Ruhn Danaan and Baxian Argos are taken alive and shipped to the Eternal City, where the Hind and Pollux the Hammer are given charge of them, putting Hunt back in exactly the position he spent the whole book trying to avoid. Bryce, cornered at one of the city's ancient Gates, channels Hunt's lightning through the Horn in her back and tears open a portal out of the world entirely, stepping through with the Starsword and leaving everyone she loves behind. She lands in Prythian, a world she has never heard of, and is met immediately by a winged male trailing shadows and a woman leveling a dagger that is unmistakably the Starsword's twin, the first hard evidence anyone has had of where Midgard's Fae originally came from. Elsewhere, Tharion Ketos escapes the River Queen's court by selling his service to the Viper Queen; Ithan Holstrom is left holding the truth about the Bone Quarter and his brother; and Emile Renast, powerless and finally out of reach, is safe. Celestina's gentler rule has been exposed as the Asteri's leash, and Midgard's people still have no idea their world is being farmed.
recaps.in_short: Six months after saving Crescent City, Bryce Quinlan and Hunt Athalar are pulled back into the empire's war when Cormac Donnall, the Fae prince Bryce's father betroths her to, reveals himself as an agent of the human rebel network Ophion and asks for help finding a missing boy, Emile Renast, whose captured sister was a rare lightning-wielder. The search draws in Ruhn Danaan, the mer Tharion Ketos and the exiled wolf Ithan Holstrom, and ends with the discovery that the boy has no power at all. What they uncover instead is far larger: the Asteri who rule Midgard are parasites, the firstlight that powers every city is harvested from its own people, and the souls ferried to the Bone Quarter are consumed rather than laid to rest. It is what Danika Fendyr died knowing. When Rigelus of the Asteri comes for Bryce and the Horn of Luna she carries, Cormac is killed, Hunt, Ruhn and Baxian Argos are captured and taken to the Eternal City, and Bryce opens a portal with the Horn and escapes into another world entirely, arriving in front of strangers whose blade matches her own.

recaps.text: Previously, in House of Earth and Blood: Bryce Quinlan, half human and half Fae, lived in Crescent City on Midgard, a world ruled by Vanir on behalf of the Asteri, the immortal rulers seated in the Eternal City. She came home one night to find her best friend, the wolf Alpha Danika Fendyr, and Danika's entire pack slaughtered, apparently by a demon, and a human rebel was convicted of it. Two years later the killings resumed. Micah Domitus, the Archangel governing Valbara, ordered Bryce to investigate alongside Hunt Athalar, an enslaved fallen angel called the Umbra Mortis who was promised his freedom in exchange for the killer. The trail ran through a synthetic drug called synth, a demon bred to hunt by scent, and the theft of the Horn of Luna, a broken Fae artifact that can open passages between worlds. Micah proved to be the murderer: he had killed Danika for stealing the Horn and staged the later deaths to force it into the open. Danika had hidden it by grinding it into the ink of the tattoo down Bryce's back. When Micah opened a rift above the city and demons poured through, Bryce ran the city's ancient Gates, used Hunt's lightning to wake the Horn in her skin, and revealed herself as Starborn, sealing the rift and healing much of the damage. Micah died. So did Sandriel, the visiting Archangel Hunt killed rather than be sold to her, and Lehabah, the fire sprite who burned herself out defending Bryce. Bryce made the Drop into her full power with Hunt as her Anchor, and Hunt was freed. Bryce is now a publicly acknowledged Fae princess and Starborn heir, still carrying the Horn, watched by her father the Autumn King, by the Asteri, and by the Princes of Hel, while the empire's war against the human rebel network Ophion grinds on across the sea.

Six months after the battle for Crescent City, Bryce and Hunt are living together and trying to be ordinary: she at the gallery, he flying patrols with the 33rd under the new Governor, the Archangel Celestina, who is mild where Micah was merciless. Across the sea the empire's war with the human rebel network Ophion continues. A young rebel named Sofie Renast, a thunderbird whose lightning the Asteri hunt on sight, is captured by the Hind, the empire's spymaster, after breaking into a labor camp to reach her younger brother, Emile. Bryce's father, the Autumn King, betroths her without warning to Cormac Donnall, Prince of Avallen. Cormac wants the engagement no more than she does: he is an Ophion agent, Sofie was his lover, and he has come to Crescent City to find Emile before the empire does. He asks Bryce and Ruhn for help. Ithan Holstrom, newly cast out by the wolves, is meanwhile living on their couch.

The search for Emile Renast draws in half the city. Tharion Ketos is ordered by the River Queen to find the boy first, on terms he is not permitted to refuse. Ruhn takes his instructions from Ophion through an anonymous mind-to-mind contact who calls herself Daybright and will reveal nothing about who she is. Bryce, needing a way to trace someone nobody can find, goes to the Astronomer, who keeps three drugged mystics floating in tanks and rents out their sight. Ithan is trying to learn what happened to his brother Connor's soul after the massacre, and finds the keepers of the Bone Quarter unwilling to answer anything. The Asteri's arranged marriage between Governor Celestina and the young Witch-Queen Hypaxia Enador is announced, with neither woman consulted.

Cormac presses the group to earn Ophion's trust by taking part in its operations, and Hunt, who has more to lose than any of them, resists being dragged back into a rebellion that already cost him two centuries. The rebels are not one thing: Pippa Spetsos, who commands Ophion's Lightfall squadron, treats every Vanir as a target and unnerves her own allies. Bryce keeps working on what the Horn in her back can actually do and on what being Starborn means, questions the Fae will not answer honestly. Baxian Argos, the angel called the Helhound and once Sandriel's, has transferred to Crescent City and takes an interest in Bryce and Hunt that none of them can explain. Traces of Danika keep surfacing where they should not: she had been in contact with people she never mentioned.

An Ophion raid the group is drawn into ends in slaughter, with imperial forces waiting where they should not have been, and the question of who informed poisons everything afterward. The empire's response falls on Crescent City, and the limits of Celestina's gentler rule become plain. Bryce establishes that Danika had been in contact with Sofie Renast before either of them died, and that whatever Danika learned about the Asteri was worth dying to protect. Emile's trail leads out of the city toward the marshes and lakes beyond it, with Ophion, the empire, the River Queen and the Meat Market all converging on a boy none of them has ever met.

Emile is found, and the premise everyone has been fighting over collapses: the boy has no power at all. Sofie was the thunderbird, and she protected her brother by letting the world believe the gift was his. Sofie herself is confirmed dead. Tharion, ordered to deliver the boy to the River Queen, has to decide what he is willing to do for a monarch who does not accept refusals. Bryce, Hunt and Ruhn are left holding a rebellion's worth of trouble with nothing to show for it, while imperial pressure on the city keeps increasing and Cormac's grief makes him reckless.

Baxian reveals why he has been circling Bryce and Hunt: Danika was his mate, and he has spent two years quietly trying to finish what she started. What Danika had been investigating comes into focus, and it is not a drug ring or a stolen artifact but the Asteri themselves. Aidas, a Prince of Hel, tells Bryce that she descends from Theia, a Starborn queen, and that Hel's long war was never against Midgard but against the Asteri, who are not gods but parasites feeding on the world's magic. Ithan, coming at the same wall from a different direction, finds that the answers about the Bone Quarter are worse than the silence was.

The truth about how Midgard is powered comes out. Firstlight, the energy running every city on the planet, is harvested from the Vanir themselves, and the Bone Quarter is not a resting place: the souls ferried across the Istros are consumed, their secondlight drained into the same system. Every funeral the city has ever held was a delivery. Ithan learns what that means for his brother. Bryce, Hunt and Ruhn now understand what Danika discovered and why the empire killed to bury it, and Rigelus, the Bright Hand of the Asteri, begins taking a direct and personal interest in Bryce and in the Horn she carries.

With the scale of the lie established, the group has to decide what to do with it. Ophion fractures: Pippa's Lightfall squadron seizes the imperial war machines the rebels stole and demonstrates how little it cares who dies. The empire tightens its hold on Crescent City, and Celestina's position between the Asteri and the people she governs becomes untenable. Bryce works out that the Horn in her back, woken by Hunt's lightning, can do more than seal a rift: it can open one. Rigelus moves pieces toward Lunathion, and everyone close to Bryce becomes leverage against her.

The Asteri come for Bryce. Rigelus, having identified her as both the Starborn heir and the vessel carrying the Horn, arrives to collect her, and the city's defenses count for nothing against him. Hunt, Ruhn, Cormac and Baxian fight a battle they cannot win. Cormac dies. The rebellion in Valbara is broken and its cells rolled up, the Hind's work done thoroughly. Bryce's only remaining advantages are the artifact in her skin and the light in her blood, and she prepares to spend both.

Cornered at the Old Square Gate with the Asteri closing in, Bryce uses Hunt's lightning to wake the Horn inked into her back and tears open a portal to somewhere else entirely. Hunt, Ruhn and Baxian are taken alive and shipped to the Eternal City to be broken by the Hind and the Hammer, and there is nothing Bryce can do for them from where she is standing. She goes through the portal. She lands in another world, in a place she has never seen, facing a winged male trailing shadows and a woman who levels a blade at her that is unmistakably the twin of the Starsword she carries. Behind her, Crescent City is under the Asteri's heel; ahead of her are strangers whose weapons match her own.

characters.description: The High King of Elfhame, and the subject of this collection of tales. The youngest and least wanted son of the old High King, he grew up with no household of his own and no one who would claim him, and he made himself notorious rather than be overlooked. He now holds a throne he never expected to keep, married to a mortal queen, and he is surrounded by stories about who he is and what he did, most of which were told about him long before he had any say in them.
characters.name: Cardan

characters.description: The mortal High Queen of Elfhame, Cardan's wife and co-ruler, raised in Faerie by the general who murdered her parents and now holding a throne no human was ever supposed to hold. In the present-day sections of the book she is the one person who knows Cardan without reference to his reputation.
characters.name: Jude Duarte

characters.description: Cardan's mother, a courtier who bore the High King's youngest child and gained nothing by it. Told that her son was fated to bring ruin on the crown, and finding him no use to her ambitions, she gave him neither care nor a place, and the boy was left to be passed around a court that had no interest in him.
characters.name: Lady Asha

characters.description: The old High King of Elfhame, Cardan's father, who ruled for centuries and had many children. Warned by prophecy about his youngest, he kept the boy landless, titleless and at arm's length, neither raising him nor casting him out.
characters.name: High King Eldred

characters.description: Cardan's eldest brother, who eventually took the unwanted boy into his own household. What he offered was not affection but instruction: a home run on cruelty, where power was demonstrated by what one could do to those with none. Much of what the court later found monstrous in Cardan he learned there.
characters.name: Prince Balekin

recaps.ending: The collection closes in the present, with Cardan settled on a throne he was never meant to hold and Jude beside him as High Queen. Nothing in the earlier tales is undone by it: the neglected child, the boy raised in his brother's violent household, and the notorious young prince are plainly the same person as the king, and the court's stories about him are not lies so much as accounts written by people who were never going to give him the benefit of the doubt. The book's argument, made through the sequence rather than stated, is that a story told about someone before they can answer becomes a cage, and that Cardan's hatred of stories is the hatred of a person who was defined by them from birth. What has changed is that he is no longer alone inside them: the marriage holds, the reign holds, and he now has both the power to make his own account and one person who does not need the account to know him. The trilogy's outcome is left standing, and the novella ends as a companion piece to it rather than a continuation, filling in the childhood that the main books only glanced at.
recaps.in_short: A short companion volume to the Folk of the Air trilogy, gathering linked tales about Cardan, told from outside his own point of view and framed by his present life as High King of Elfhame with Jude as his queen. The stories go back to his birth, to the prophecy that the old High King's youngest son would bring ruin on the crown, and to a mother who saw no advantage in him and a father who kept him landless and unclaimed. They follow a child nobody would take responsibility for, his eventual place in the household of his eldest brother Balekin, who taught cruelty as a form of authority, and the notorious, idle young prince the court came to gossip about. Set against these are the present-day sections, in which the same person wears the crown and lives with a reputation assembled by people who were never fair to him. The book takes its title from that: Cardan distrusts stories because stories about him were told long before he had any say in them.

recaps.text: Previously, in the Folk of the Air trilogy: mortal twins Jude and Taryn Duarte were raised in Faerie by Madoc, the redcap general who killed their parents. Jude fought for a place at the High Court, spied for Prince Dain, and was tormented by Prince Cardan, the High King's youngest son. When Prince Balekin murdered the High King and most of his heirs with Madoc's help, Jude captured Cardan, the last heir able to pass the crown, and made him High King in exchange for his oath to obey her for a year and a day, keeping her small brother Oak, the secret true heir, out of Madoc's reach. Ruling as Cardan's seneschal, Jude survived assassins, Madoc's plotting and captivity in the Undersea. When Madoc moved against the throne, Cardan married her, making her High Queen, and then exiled her to the mortal world. She returned in her twin's place after Locke's death, the marriage was acknowledged, and in the final confrontation an old prophecy attached to Cardan's birth was fulfilled: he was turned into a serpent that ravaged the court, and Jude killed it, restoring him. Madoc was defeated and exiled, and Jude and Cardan now rule Elfhame together. This novella looks back at Cardan's own history.

The book opens the way a book of tales does, presenting the High King of Elfhame as a figure other people tell stories about, and then going back to where those stories start. Cardan was the last of the old High King's children, born to a court lady, Asha, who expected the birth to raise her standing and found that it did not. A prophecy attached itself to him at once: this son would bring ruin on the crown of Elfhame. His father, Eldred, responded by keeping him at a distance, giving him no lands, no title and no household, and his mother, having no use for a child who could not advance her, gave him no care either. The early tales follow a boy who belonged to nobody in a palace full of people who all knew exactly what had been foretold about him, and who learned young that attention, of any kind, was easier to get than affection.

The middle tales cover the years that made the prince the court gossiped about. Cardan is eventually taken into the household of his eldest brother, Balekin, which is the closest thing to a home he is offered and is run on violence: Balekin's method of raising him is to demonstrate that authority means being able to hurt people who cannot hurt you back, and to punish any sign that the lesson has not been absorbed. What the court sees from outside is a landless youngest prince with no responsibilities, a talent for spectacle and a habit of cruelty, and it tells the appropriate stories about him. The tales sit that outside view against what produced it, and the present-day sections, in which the same man now holds the crown and is married to a mortal queen, show him living with a reputation he can neither disprove nor entirely disown.

The final tales bring the sequence up to the present and close it. Cardan is High King of Elfhame, ruling with Jude as High Queen, and the collection's separate strands, the prophecy, the mother who would not claim him, the father who would not either, the brother who taught him what power looked like, resolve into a single account of how the boy became the man on the throne. The book does not rehabilitate him; the cruelties in the earlier stories are left as they were. What it does is show why a person who has been narrated all his life by people with no interest in being fair to him would come to hate stories, which is where the title lands. It ends with Cardan in a position none of the prophecies allowed for: still the subject of everyone else's tales, but no longer alone in them, and finally in a position to act rather than to be described.

characters.description: The undersized heir of the Hairy Hooligan tribe on Berk, now an initiated member of it after the events of the first book. He is still small, still thoughtful, and still the worst fighter of his year, particularly with a sword. His one real advantage, the ability to speak Dragonese, is something he continues to keep largely to himself.
characters.name: Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III

characters.description: Hiccup's dragon, a very small, toothless Common or Garden dragon who is greedy, vain, disobedient and inclined to lie about it. He goes where Hiccup goes, mostly under his shirt, and complains about it.
characters.name: Toothless

characters.description: Hiccup's closest friend: skinny, nervous, allergic to reptiles and no better with a sword than Hiccup is. He expects things to go wrong and generally says so.
characters.name: Fishlegs

characters.description: Hiccup's cousin and rival for the chieftainship, strong, loud and openly scornful of him, and quick to take any opportunity to make him look ridiculous.
characters.name: Snotface Snotlout

characters.description: Snotlout's enormous and slow-witted companion, who provides the muscle for his bullying.
characters.name: Dogsbreath the Duhbrain

characters.description: Chief of the Hairy Hooligans and Hiccup's father, a huge and noisy man with a strong Viking appetite for treasure hunting.
characters.name: Stoick the Vast

characters.description: The tribe's vast, bellowing instructor, who is teaching Hiccup's year to fight with swords and regards Hiccup's efforts as a personal insult.
characters.name: Gobber the Belch

characters.description: A half-drowned stranger the Hooligans find alive inside the coffin that washes ashore at Berk. He introduces himself as a farmer down on his luck, is grateful, agreeable and full of admiration for his rescuers, and takes an unusually close interest in the treasure map that comes ashore with him.
characters.name: Alvin the Poor-but-Honest Farmer

characters.description: The most feared Viking pirate who ever lived, dead long before the story begins and an ancestor of Hiccup's. His coffin, the riddle he left behind and the treasure he is supposed to have hidden are what set the whole voyage in motion.
characters.name: Grimbeard the Ghastly

characters.description: Chief of the Meathead tribe, a neighbour and sometime ally of Stoick's, and equally unable to resist the promise of a treasure hunt.
characters.name: Mogadon the Meathead

characters.description: Mogadon's son and heir, a capable boy of about Hiccup's age and one of the very few outside Berk who treats Hiccup as worth speaking to rather than as a joke.
characters.name: Thuggory the Meathead

recaps.ending: Hiccup faces Alvin the Treacherous with a sword in Grimbeard the Ghastly's tomb and comes out of it alive, which nobody who has watched him in Gobber's lessons would have predicted. The hoard is not recovered: Hiccup, Fishlegs and Toothless get off the island with their lives and very little else, and the Hooligans sail home exactly as poor as they left. Alvin is left behind and is taken for dead, an assumption the story does not encourage the reader to trust. Hiccup's standing in the tribe is a little better than it was, but nothing fundamental has changed at home: Snotlout is unaltered, Stoick still has no idea that his son's real advantage is being able to talk to dragons, and Toothless is as impossible as ever. Grimbeard the Ghastly, and what he left behind him, are unfinished business for the books that follow.
recaps.in_short: A coffin washes ashore at Berk during a sword-fighting lesson.
