It carries the name of Grimbeard the Ghastly, the most feared Viking pirate who ever lived and an ancestor of Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III, and it holds two things: a living man, a shipwrecked stranger who calls himself Alvin the Poor-but-Honest Farmer, and the trail to Grimbeard's lost treasure. The Hairy Hooligans and the Meatheads set out after it, to an island guarded by Skullions, blind dragons that hunt by scent and cannot be fought. Hiccup, the only one able to make sense of the riddle, reaches the tomb ahead of the adults with Fishlegs and Toothless, and there the stranger shows himself for what he is: Alvin the Treacherous, who wants the hoard and no witnesses. Hiccup, the worst swordsman of his year, survives the duel. The treasure is lost, Alvin is left for dead, and the Hooligans come home no richer than they went.

recaps.text: Previously: Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III is the undersized son of Stoick the Vast, chief of the Hairy Hooligan tribe on the island of Berk, and the tribe's unlikely heir. In the first book he scraped through the tribe's initiation with the least impressive dragon on the island, a tiny toothless Common or Garden dragon he named Toothless, and then saved Berk from a monstrous stranded sea dragon using the one skill nobody else has: he can speak Dragonese, the dragons' own language, in a tribe convinced that yelling is the only way to handle a dragon. His friend Fishlegs is anxious and allergic to reptiles; his cousin Snotlout still despises him and still expects to be chief one day. Hiccup is an accepted Hooligan now, but he is no bigger, no louder and no better at the violent things Vikings admire, and he keeps his talent for talking to dragons mostly to himself.

Hiccup's year is being taught to fight with swords by Gobber the Belch, and Hiccup is the worst in the class by a wide margin. During the lesson a coffin drifts ashore. It carries the name of Grimbeard the Ghastly, the most feared Viking pirate who ever lived and an ancestor of Hiccup's, and inside it the Hooligans find a half-drowned man who is still alive, a stranger calling himself Alvin the Poor-but-Honest Farmer, together with the pirate's belongings. Among them is the trail to the treasure Grimbeard is said to have hidden before he died. Nothing appeals to a Viking tribe more than lost treasure, and Stoick begins organising an expedition.

The Hooligans set out after Grimbeard's treasure in company with the Meathead tribe under Mogadon the Meathead, whose son Thuggory is one of the few boys outside Berk to treat Hiccup decently. The trail is not a straightforward one, and it leads to an island the tribes avoid, guarded by Skullions: blind, armoured dragons that hunt by smell and are not worth fighting. Alvin attaches himself to the expedition and takes a close interest both in the map and in Hiccup, who is the only person able to make sense of the riddle written on it. Hiccup, Fishlegs and Toothless end up ahead of the adults and inside the island's tunnels.

Underground, Hiccup, Fishlegs and Toothless find their way to Grimbeard the Ghastly's tomb and the hoard he was buried with. Alvin reaches it as well, and drops the pretence of being a poor but honest farmer. He is Alvin the Treacherous, he has been after the treasure from the moment he came ashore, and he intends to leave no one behind to argue about it. Hiccup, the worst swordsman of his year, is the one left facing him.

Hiccup fights Alvin in the tomb and, to his own astonishment as much as anyone else's, survives the duel. The treasure does not come home with them: it is lost along with the tomb, and the boys escape the island with their lives and nothing more. Alvin is left behind and is taken for dead, which proves to be premature. Hiccup returns to Berk no richer than he left it, having again done something none of the adults expected of him, and the Hooligans go back to being one of the poorest tribes in the archipelago.

characters.description: The small and thoughtful heir of the Hairy Hooligans. Hiccup can speak Dragonese and has survived dangers far beyond his tribe's training, but he is still most likely to enter danger because a friend needs him.
characters.name: Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III

characters.description: Hiccup's tiny Common or Garden dragon, greedy, vain and loudly unwilling to risk himself. His attachment to Hiccup is stronger than his complaints suggest.
characters.name: Toothless

characters.description: Hiccup's oldest friend, an anxious, short-sighted Viking boy who was found as a baby and knows very little about his birth family.
characters.name: Fishlegs

characters.description: Hiccup's fearless Bog-Burglar friend and an expert thief. Her disappearance during a storm sends both tribes searching for her.
characters.name: Camicazi

characters.description: Chief of the Hairy Hooligans and Hiccup's father, a huge warrior who leads his people into the search for Camicazi.
characters.name: Stoick the Vast

characters.description: Chief of the Bog-Burglars and Camicazi's mother. Bertha is a formidable leader who will not leave her missing daughter unfound.
characters.name: Big-Boobied Bertha

characters.description: The large flying dragon that carried Hiccup home through the great storm of the previous book. Once too frightened to fly, the Windwalker now follows Hiccup by choice.
characters.name: the Windwalker

characters.description: Hiccup's old enemy, scarred by earlier defeats but still alive and still determined to use Hiccup for his own plans.
characters.name: Alvin the Treacherous

characters.description: A clever and dangerous witch working with Alvin. She knows old stories and family secrets and uses that knowledge to set traps for Hiccup and his friends.
characters.name: the Witch

characters.description: A powerful three-headed dragon encountered on Berserk. The Deadly Shadow is dangerous, intelligent and driven by a long attachment to a human it once served.
characters.name: the Deadly Shadow

characters.description: Fishlegs's mother, known through the story of the choices she made to protect her baby. Her connection with the Deadly Shadow finally gives Fishlegs part of the family history he has never had.
characters.name: Termagant

characters.description: The fierce inhabitants of the island of Berserk, feared by the other Viking tribes and ready to make prisoners of strangers who enter their territory.
characters.name: the Berserks

recaps.ending: Hiccup and Fishlegs find Camicazi and escape the dangers of Berserk with her. Alvin and the Witch's trap does not give them control of Hiccup, although both enemies remain part of the larger threat around him. The journey also answers a question Fishlegs has carried all his life. The three-headed Deadly Shadow was bound to his mother, Termagant, and its recognition of Fishlegs preserves the link between them after her death. Fishlegs cannot recover the family he lost as a baby, but he learns that he was loved and protected rather than simply abandoned. The Deadly Shadow accepts him and leaves with the children. Camicazi returns to her mother and tribe, while Hiccup comes home with both friends alive. The old history uncovered on Berserk leaves Hiccup with more reason to distrust Alvin and the Witch and with a clearer sense that their plans reach into the past of the archipelago.
recaps.in_short: When Camicazi disappears in a storm, Hiccup, Fishlegs and the two tribes join the search. The trail leads to the feared island of Berserk, where strangers are taken prisoner and old secrets have been turned into traps. Hiccup and Fishlegs become separated from their families, encounter a dangerous three-headed dragon called the Deadly Shadow and discover that Alvin the Treacherous is working with a powerful Witch. The enemies want to use Hiccup and the history surrounding him, while Camicazi remains in danger. The Deadly Shadow's story becomes part of Fishlegs's own: it once belonged to his mother, Termagant, who protected him when he was a baby. Hiccup and his friends escape, Camicazi is rescued, and Fishlegs leaves with the knowledge that his mother loved him and with the Deadly Shadow as a living link to her. Alvin and the Witch survive to threaten them again.

recaps.text: Previously: Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III is the unlikely heir of the Hairy Hooligans, a small boy who can secretly speak Dragonese and repeatedly survives by understanding what other Vikings attack. His closest companions are Toothless, Fishlegs and Camicazi. In the last book the three children were swept out of an inter-tribal swimming race, crossed the western ocean and reached the land Viking maps said did not exist. A frightened Windwalker dragon repaid Hiccup's kindness by carrying him home through a great storm. Hiccup defeated his enemy Norbert and reached the race finish in time. Alvin the Treacherous, an enemy from earlier adventures, has never been safely accounted for.

A violent storm separates Camicazi from the others, and she does not return. Big-Boobied Bertha and Stoick lead their tribes in a search, while Hiccup and Fishlegs refuse to believe that their friend is simply lost. The trail points toward waters and islands that sensible Vikings avoid. Hiccup has the Windwalker as well as Toothless, but even a flying dragon cannot make the weather or the search safe. Finding Camicazi means continuing toward Berserk, a place surrounded by frightening stories and old hostility.

The search reaches Berserk, where the island's inhabitants treat newcomers as enemies and prisoners. Hiccup and Fishlegs are cut off from the safety of their tribes and must keep looking for Camicazi while trying to avoid capture themselves. They encounter the Deadly Shadow, a huge three-headed dragon with a fierce loyalty rooted in its past. It is too intelligent to be dismissed as a simple monster, and its unusual interest in Fishlegs suggests that the island holds more than the answer to Camicazi's disappearance.

Alvin the Treacherous is alive and has joined forces with a dangerous Witch. They have used the secrets and fears surrounding Berserk to draw Hiccup into a trap. Camicazi is caught in the same scheme, so escape cannot come at the cost of leaving her behind. The Witch knows old history that Hiccup does not, while the Deadly Shadow's behaviour begins to reveal a separate secret about Fishlegs. The dragon is connected to the parent Fishlegs never knew, and its loyalty may be the one advantage Alvin and the Witch did not plan for.

Hiccup and Fishlegs rescue Camicazi and break out of the trap on Berserk. The Deadly Shadow helps rather than hunts them because it recognises Fishlegs's connection to its former human companion. That companion was Termagant, Fishlegs's mother, who acted to protect him when he was a baby. Fishlegs learns that he was loved and gains the Deadly Shadow as a link to the family he lost. The three children escape and Camicazi returns to Big-Boobied Bertha. Alvin and the Witch are not permanently defeated, and the old knowledge they possess remains dangerous, but they fail to take Hiccup or destroy his friendship with the others.

characters.description: The small and unimpressive heir of the Hairy Hooligan tribe on Berk, who can speak Dragonese and still tells almost nobody. He is a poor fighter and an indifferent Viking by his tribe's standards, and is generally the person who notices what everyone else has missed.
characters.name: Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III

characters.description: Hiccup's dragon: tiny, toothless, greedy and entirely disobedient, with a talent for making a bad situation worse and a habit of explaining, in Dragonese, why none of it is his fault.
characters.name: Toothless

characters.description: Hiccup's oldest friend: skinny, short-sighted, allergic to reptiles and reliably pessimistic. He has been at the bottom of the class alongside Hiccup since the initiation programme.
characters.name: Fishlegs

characters.description: The Bog-Burglar girl Hiccup and Fishlegs met while imprisoned by the Romans: very small, very blonde, an exceptional thief and lock-picker, and not deterred by an errand everyone else considers impossible.
characters.name: Camicazi

characters.description: Chief of the Hairy Hooligans and Hiccup's father, huge, loud and inclined to meet a problem head on.
characters.name: Stoick the Vast

characters.description: The Hooligans' enormous instructor and drill-master, a fixture of tribe life on Berk.
characters.name: Gobber the Belch

characters.description: Hiccup's cousin and rival, strong, loud and contemptuous of him.
characters.name: Snotface Snotlout

characters.description: Hiccup's grandfather and the tribe's elderly soothsayer, whose knowledge of old lore and older stories is what turns a hopeless case into a journey with a destination.
characters.name: Old Wrinkly

characters.description: A small dragon whose bite carries a poison that brings on Vorpentitis, an illness the Hooligans have no treatment for and which kills to a predictable timetable.
characters.name: the Venomous Vorpent

characters.description: Chief of the Hysterics, the least hospitable tribe in the archipelago. He carries a battleaxe and swings without warning between polite conversation and homicidal rage, and his tribe's usual policy towards visitors is to kill them.
characters.name: Norbert the Nutjob

characters.description: An enormous sea dragon that patrols the waters around the Hysterics' island, and a large part of the reason nobody goes there.
characters.name: the Doomfang

characters.description: Norbert's father, who sailed west beyond the known seas and came back with the strange vegetable the Hysterics have kept as a treasure ever since.
characters.name: Bigfoot Bjornsson

recaps.ending: Hiccup, Camicazi and Toothless get off Hysteria with the stolen potato, survive the crossing and the Doomfang, and reach Berk before the poison has finished its work. Fishlegs eats the cure and recovers from Vorpentitis. Very few people on Berk ever learn how any of it was managed. Norbert the Nutjob comes out of the affair alive, minus the sacred object his father brought back from the west and with a fixed personal hatred of Hiccup, which makes him the enemy carried forward into the next book. Nothing about Hiccup's own position changes: he is still the smallest and least Viking-like member of his tribe, still keeps Dragonese to himself, and still has a dragon who takes instruction from nobody. His friendship with Camicazi and Fishlegs is the one thing the book leaves visibly stronger than it found it.
recaps.in_short: Fishlegs is bitten by a Venomous Vorpent and contracts Vorpentitis, a poisoning that kills to a schedule and for which there is exactly one cure: a potato, a vegetable unheard of in the archipelago, of which the only known specimen is a sacred relic of the Hysterics. Their island is frozen in, guarded by the sea dragon called the Doomfang, and ruled by Norbert the Nutjob, who kills visitors as a matter of course. Hiccup and Camicazi sail there anyway with Toothless. They are caught and brought in front of Norbert, Camicazi steals the potato, and the escape becomes a chase across the ice and the open sea with the Doomfang in it. Hiccup gets home in time and Fishlegs is cured. Norbert survives, having lost his tribe's treasure, and takes up a grudge against Hiccup that outlasts the book.

recaps.text: Previously: Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III is the undersized heir of the Hairy Hooligan tribe on Berk, still nothing like the Viking his father Stoick the Vast hoped for, and still quiet about the one thing that makes him remarkable, which is that he can speak Dragonese. His dragon Toothless is a small, greedy, disobedient Common or Garden dragon. His friends are Fishlegs, anxious and allergic to reptiles, and Camicazi, a tiny Bog-Burglar girl and expert thief he met while a prisoner of the Romans in the previous book. Hiccup has already saved Berk from a monstrous sea dragon, been down into the tomb of his pirate ancestor Grimbeard the Ghastly, and twice come off better than Alvin the Treacherous, who is still alive and still an enemy.

Fishlegs is bitten by a Venomous Vorpent, a small dragon whose poison brings on Vorpentitis. The illness is reliably fatal and it works to a timetable, so Fishlegs has days rather than weeks, and nothing the Hooligans know how to do will help him. There is one cure, and it is barely more than a rumour: a vegetable unknown in the archipelago, a potato, and the only one in existence belongs to the Hysterics. Their island lies behind frozen seas, it is guarded by the Doomfang, and their chief, Norbert the Nutjob, is not a man from whom anything can be politely requested. Hiccup and Camicazi set out for it regardless.

Hiccup, Camicazi and Toothless make the winter crossing to Hysteria with the time left to Fishlegs running down behind them. The Hysterics do not receive visitors so much as dispose of them, and Norbert the Nutjob shifts between civility and murderous fury without warning. The potato is not lying about to be picked up either: it was brought back from a voyage west by Norbert's father, Bigfoot Bjornsson, and the Hysterics treat it as a holy object. Taking it will need Camicazi's burgling rather than any kind of negotiation.

Hiccup and Camicazi are taken by the Hysterics and brought in front of Norbert the Nutjob, who is entirely willing to kill them and requires very little excuse. Camicazi gets the potato out of Hysteric hands, but the theft is discovered, and from that point Norbert's interest in Hiccup becomes personal. The escape runs from the Hysterics' hall out onto the ice and into the freezing sea, where the Doomfang is waiting and where the cold is as dangerous as the pursuit, while what is left of Fishlegs's time keeps shrinking.

Hiccup gets away from Hysteria with the potato, though not without ending up in the sea and face to face with the Doomfang, and reaches Berk in time. Fishlegs eats the cure and recovers from the Vorpentitis. Norbert the Nutjob survives the chase, having lost his tribe's most precious possession to a Hooligan boy, and comes out of it with a personal grudge against Hiccup that he intends to pursue for as long as it takes; he becomes the standing enemy of the books that follow. Hiccup comes home having done something no adult on Berk would have attempted, and, as usual, without much of his tribe understanding how he did it.

characters.description: The undersized heir of the Hairy Hooligans, a thoughtful boy in a world that admires noise and muscle. Hiccup speaks Dragonese, keeps that gift mostly secret and has learned that helping a frightened dragon can matter more than commanding it.
characters.name: Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III

characters.description: Hiccup's tiny Common or Garden dragon, greedy, stubborn and usually unwilling to do anything simply because Hiccup asks.
characters.name: Toothless

characters.description: Hiccup's oldest friend, short-sighted, anxious and allergic to reptiles. Fishlegs dislikes both cold water and reckless plans but will not leave his friends to face either alone.
characters.name: Fishlegs

characters.description: A young Bog-Burglar, expert thief and fearless companion to Hiccup and Fishlegs. Camicazi approaches a dangerous race with much more enthusiasm than either boy.
characters.name: Camicazi

characters.description: Chief of the Hairy Hooligans and Hiccup's father, enormous, proud and certain that a Viking competition should be settled by strength.
characters.name: Stoick the Vast

characters.description: Chief of the Bog-Burglars and Camicazi's mother, a powerful leader who enters tribal contests with complete confidence in her side.
characters.name: Big-Boobied Bertha

characters.description: Chief of the Murderous Tribe and one of the dangerous adults involved in the inter-tribal swimming contest.
characters.name: Madguts the Murderous

characters.description: Chief of the Hysterics and an old enemy of Hiccup. Norbert can change from friendly talk to murderous anger without warning and has not forgotten the potato stolen from his tribe.
characters.name: Norbert the Nutjob

characters.description: A badly frightened flying dragon that Hiccup meets during the voyage. The Windwalker has strength and speed hidden beneath its fear, and Hiccup refuses to treat it as useless simply because it cannot yet fly when ordered.
characters.name: the Windwalker

characters.description: Hiccup's boastful cousin and rival, strong in the sort of public Viking competition that makes Hiccup look weakest.
characters.name: Snotface Snotlout

recaps.ending: After reaching the western land that the Vikings believed did not exist, Hiccup, Fishlegs and Camicazi still have to cross the ocean and meet the three-month deadline of the swimming race. Norbert's treachery and the great storm make the return as dangerous as the outward voyage. The Windwalker, which Hiccup protected when it was frightened and unable to fly, finally trusts him and carries him through the storm. Hiccup reaches the finish in time and wins the contest in the most unlikely way possible: by riding a dragon after a race that began in the sea. His friends return safely, Norbert is defeated, and the journey brings back proof that there is land beyond the known ocean. The Windwalker remains attached to Hiccup, giving him a larger flying companion alongside Toothless and rewarding the kindness he showed when the dragon seemed broken.
recaps.in_short: An inter-tribal swimming race sends Hiccup, Fishlegs and Camicazi into the sea, where the contest quickly becomes a real struggle for survival. They are carried far from the course and fall into the hands of Norbert the Nutjob, the Hysteric chief who still wants revenge on Hiccup. The voyage continues west across the unknown ocean. Along the way Hiccup protects a terrified Windwalker dragon that seems unable to fly, while Norbert's plans make it uncertain whether any of the children will return. They reach the western land that Viking maps say does not exist, but must still get home before the race's three-month limit. In the final storm the Windwalker finds its courage, carries Hiccup through the sky and helps him reach the finish in time. Hiccup wins, his friends survive and the voyage proves that a whole land lies beyond the familiar archipelago.

recaps.text: Previously: Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III is the small and unconventional heir of the Hairy Hooligans on Berk. He can speak Dragonese and travels with his troublesome little dragon Toothless. His closest friends are Fishlegs and Camicazi. Hiccup has saved Vikings from sea dragons, Romans, Alvin the Treacherous, Vorpentitis, fire dragons and a volcanic eruption. He has also entered the forbidden Meathead Public Library and used its hidden knowledge to add to his own guide to dragonkind. Norbert the Nutjob, chief of the Hysterics, has hated Hiccup since Hiccup stole the Hysterics' sacred potato to save Fishlegs.

The Hairy Hooligans, Bog-Burglars and Murderous Tribe gather for an inter-tribal swimming race. Hiccup is at an immediate disadvantage: he is smaller and weaker than most Viking competitors, while the adults treat the dangerous event as friendly sport. Hiccup, Fishlegs and Camicazi are swept away from the expected course. What should have been a race near home becomes a journey into open water with no easy way back. The rules allow three months before the contest is finally over, but surviving the sea is now more urgent than winning.

The three children are carried farther from Berk and encounter Norbert the Nutjob. Norbert has not forgiven Hiccup for the theft of the potato that cured Fishlegs, and any help he appears to offer cannot be trusted. The voyage turns westward into waters that the Vikings barely know. Hiccup also meets a Windwalker dragon made helpless by fear. Rather than abandon or bully it, he treats it as a creature that may recover. As the distance from home grows, the three-month deadline becomes a nearly impossible target.

Hiccup, Fishlegs and Camicazi cross the great western ocean and reach a land their own people believe does not exist. The discovery proves that earlier stories of voyages beyond the Viking world were true. It does not make the children safe: Norbert remains dangerous, supplies and transport are uncertain, and the race clock is still running on the other side of the sea. Hiccup has to plan a return across the same enormous distance. The Windwalker stays near him, but its fear of flight means he cannot yet rely on it for the journey home.

The return voyage becomes a race against both Norbert and a huge storm. Hiccup's earlier kindness to the Windwalker proves decisive: the dragon overcomes its fear, accepts Hiccup as a rider and carries him through weather no swimmer or ship could beat. Fishlegs and Camicazi make it back safely, Norbert is defeated, and Hiccup reaches the finish before the three-month limit expires. He wins the swimming race by arriving on a dragon, an answer no conventional competitor had imagined. He also brings home proof of the western land and gains the loyalty of the Windwalker, whose courage has grown alongside his own.

characters.description: The small, thoughtful heir of the Hairy Hooligan tribe on Berk, no better with a sword than he was and no closer to being the sort of Viking his father wants. He can speak Dragonese, the dragons' own language, which he learned by listening and which he still treats as a private matter rather than an accomplishment.
characters.name: Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III

characters.description: Hiccup's dragon: a tiny, toothless Common or Garden dragon, greedy, contrary and self-important, who obeys instructions only when it suits him and argues about everything in Dragonese.
characters.name: Toothless

characters.description: Hiccup's friend since the initiation programme: thin, anxious, allergic to reptiles, and convinced that whatever is about to happen will be bad. He is usually the one dragged along on Hiccup's disasters.
characters.name: Fishlegs

characters.description: Chief of the Hairy Hooligans and Hiccup's father, enormous, loud and quick to fight, especially with the chief of the Bog-Burglars.
characters.name: Stoick the Vast

characters.description: The Hooligans' vast instructor, responsible for the training exercise that begins the book.
characters.name: Gobber the Belch

characters.description: Hiccup's cousin and rival for the chieftainship, strong, loud, and pleased by any humiliation of Hiccup.
characters.name: Snotface Snotlout

characters.description: The villain of the previous book, who was left for dead in Grimbeard the Ghastly's tomb and was not dead. He has attached himself to the Romans, he knows exactly who Hiccup is and what the son of a chief is worth, and he has a personal score to settle.
characters.name: Alvin the Treacherous

characters.description: The Roman officer commanding the fort, a comfortable, self-satisfied man who is in the archipelago to make money out of it. He regards Vikings as barbarians and dragons as merchandise, and takes Alvin's advice.
characters.name: the Fat Consul

characters.description: A very small, very blonde girl of about Hiccup's age, daughter of the Bog-Burglar chief and already an accomplished thief and escape artist. She is fearless to a degree that alarms even Hiccup, cannot be persuaded that any situation is hopeless, and has been trying to break out of Roman custody since she arrived in it.
characters.name: Camicazi

characters.description: Chief of the Bog-Burglar tribe and Camicazi's mother, a large and forceful woman whose tribe steals from everybody, and who cannot be in the same place as Stoick the Vast for long without a quarrel breaking out.
characters.name: Big-Boobied Bertha

recaps.ending: The Roman plan is broken, and it is Hiccup's Dragonese rather than any feat of Viking arms that undoes a scheme built on captive dragons. The Fat Consul's ambitions in the archipelago end with it. The Hooligans and the Bog-Burglars come out of the fight on the same side, more or less, although Stoick and Big-Boobied Bertha resume quarrelling at the first opportunity. Alvin the Treacherous escapes once again, badly the worse for the attempt and considerably angrier, and remains the standing enemy of the series. Camicazi's friendship with Hiccup and Fishlegs survives the escape and holds afterwards, which makes the three of them a settled group for the books that follow. At home nothing much has shifted: Hiccup is still the least likely heir on Berk, still keeps quiet about being able to talk to dragons, and still has a dragon who takes no notice of anything he says.
recaps.in_short: A training exercise in boarding an enemy ship puts Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III and Fishlegs aboard a Roman vessel, and the two boys and Toothless are taken prisoner and shut up in a Roman fort. Advising the Romans is Alvin the Treacherous, who survived the previous book and knows precisely who Hiccup is. In captivity they meet Camicazi, a tiny and fearless Bog-Burglar girl already several escape attempts into her own imprisonment, and the three of them break out together. The Romans' plans reach well beyond the fort, to the Viking tribes and to their dragons, which forces the quarrelsome Hooligans and Bog-Burglars into the same fight. Weapons are not what decides it: Hiccup's secret ability to speak Dragonese is. The Roman scheme collapses, Alvin escapes to try again, and Hiccup goes home to Berk with a new friend in Camicazi.

recaps.text: Previously: Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III is the small and unheroic heir of the Hairy Hooligan tribe on the island of Berk. He passed the tribe's initiation with a tiny, disobedient dragon called Toothless and saved Berk from a monstrous stranded sea dragon, and he has since been through a treasure hunt into the tomb of his pirate ancestor Grimbeard the Ghastly. That hunt brought him up against Alvin the Treacherous, who was left for dead in the tomb. Hiccup's one real advantage is a secret he keeps to himself: he can speak Dragonese, the dragons' own language, in a tribe that believes yelling is the only way to deal with a dragon. His friend Fishlegs is anxious and allergic to reptiles, his cousin Snotlout still despises him, and his father Stoick still hopes the boy will turn into a Viking he can boast about.

A lesson in boarding an enemy ship goes badly wrong. The vessel Hiccup and Fishlegs board is not the harmless target they were promised but a Roman ship, and the two boys and Toothless are captured and carried off to the Roman fort. The Romans are in the archipelago for profit, they are interested in dragons and in Viking hostages, and the man advising them turns out to be Alvin the Treacherous, who did not die in Grimbeard's tomb after all. Alvin knows exactly who Hiccup is, and what the son of the Hooligan chief might be worth to the Romans.

Held in the Roman fort, Hiccup and Fishlegs meet another prisoner: Camicazi, a very small Bog-Burglar girl who has already made several escape attempts and fully intends to make more. The three of them start planning a way out, with Toothless and Hiccup's Dragonese doing what brute force cannot. What they learn inside the fort matters more than their own captivity. The Romans' interest in captive dragons is part of a larger plan aimed at the Viking tribes of the archipelago, and Alvin the Treacherous is helping them with it.

The three prisoners get out of the fort, but escaping is not the end of the matter. The Roman scheme threatens the Hooligans and the Bog-Burglars alike, and both tribes are drawn in, which means Stoick the Vast and Camicazi's mother, Big-Boobied Bertha, have to cooperate despite being unable to hold a conversation without it turning into an argument. Against a plan built on captive dragons, the only tool that is any real use is the one thing Hiccup's tribe has always considered beneath a Viking: the ability to talk to dragons.

The Roman plan fails. Hiccup uses Dragonese where weapons are useless, the tribes and the dragons together turn the day against the fort, and the Fat Consul's ambitions in the archipelago come to nothing. Alvin the Treacherous escapes yet again, worse off for it and no less determined to settle with Hiccup one day. Hiccup returns to Berk with his secret still largely a secret and with a new friend: Camicazi, who from now on makes a third with him and Fishlegs. The Hooligans and Bog-Burglars part on better terms than they met, and Hiccup is no nearer to convincing his tribe that the useful thing about him is his head rather than his sword arm.

characters.description: The undersized and thoroughly unheroic son of Stoick the Vast and heir to the Hairy Hooligan tribe on the island of Berk. He is thoughtful, curious and hopeless at the shouting and brawling his tribe admires, which makes him an easy target for the other boys of his year. Unknown to almost everyone, he has taught himself to speak Dragonese by listening to dragons, a skill no Hooligan would consider worth having. The book is presented as his own memoir, written down long afterwards.
characters.name: Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III

characters.description: Hiccup's only real friend, a scrawny and anxious boy with a squint and an allergy to reptiles, which is an unfortunate condition for a Viking about to be handed a dragon. He is as unpromising a candidate for the initiation programme as Hiccup, and the two of them are at the bottom of the class together.
characters.name: Fishlegs

characters.description: Hiccup's cousin: loud, strong, well built and openly contemptuous of him. He expects to be chief of the Hairy Hooligans himself one day and loses no chance to point out that Hiccup is unfit for it. He leads the other boys in mocking Hiccup and Fishlegs throughout the initiation.
characters.name: Snotface Snotlout

characters.description: An enormous, slow-witted boy who follows Snotlout everywhere and supplies the muscle for his bullying.
characters.name: Dogsbreath the Duhbrain

characters.description: Chief of the Hairy Hooligan tribe and Hiccup's father, a vast, bellowing man whose name is announced with a warning that hearers should tremble. He badly wants his son to be an impressive heir and is embarrassed that he is not, though the fondness underneath is plain enough.
characters.name: Stoick the Vast

characters.description: The huge, roaring warrior who runs the Hairy Hooligan initiation programme and drills the ten boys of Hiccup's year. He believes in noise, obedience and doing things the way they have always been done, and holds Hiccup in very low regard.
characters.name: Gobber the Belch

characters.description: The dragon Hiccup takes from the nursery inside Wild Dragon Cliff: a very small, entirely ordinary Common or Garden dragon, and toothless besides, which makes him the least impressive catch of the whole year. He is greedy, idle, vain and disobedient, tells transparent lies, and does nothing he does not feel like doing. Because Hiccup speaks Dragonese, the two of them argue and bargain in the dragon's own language rather than through the bellowing the tribe recommends.
characters.name: Toothless

characters.description: Hiccup's grandfather and the tribe's elderly soothsayer, who reads the future in fish entrails and is one of the very few people on Berk willing to entertain the idea that there is more than one kind of hero. He listens to Hiccup and answers him in hints.
characters.name: Old Wrinkly

characters.description: The dragon Snotlout comes away with, a Monstrous Nightmare and by a wide margin the most impressive catch of the group, a fact Snotlout never allows anyone to forget.
characters.name: Fireworm

characters.description: Fishlegs's dragon, a placid Basic Brown who turns out to be a vegetarian, which Fishlegs does his best to keep quiet during training.
characters.name: Horrorcow

characters.description: A colossal sea dragon, a Seadragonus Giganticus Maximus, washed up on the shore at Berk. It is large enough to treat an entire Viking tribe as a meal, and no Hooligan weapon makes the slightest impression on it.
characters.name: the Green Death

characters.description: A second monstrous sea dragon stranded alongside the Green Death, and its natural rival. The two of them are considerably more interested in each other than in anything the Vikings on the beach can do.
characters.name: the Purple Death

recaps.ending: Two vast sea dragons, the Green Death and the Purple Death, are stranded on Berk's shore, and the tribe's weapons cannot hurt them. Hiccup, already sentenced to exile after Toothless wrecked the Thor'sday Thursday ceremony, uses his Dragonese to provoke the two monsters into turning on each other, then has the small dragons set the survivor burning from the inside, so that the gas it makes its own fire with destroys it. He is flung into the sea in the process and is pulled out half drowned by Toothless. The exile is cancelled, Fishlegs is reinstated with him, and Stoick, who has spent the whole book embarrassed by his son, declares him a hero in front of the tribe. Little else about Hiccup's life changes: Snotlout is unaltered, and Toothless is exactly as greedy and disobedient at the end as at the beginning. The story is told as the memoir of the elderly Hiccup, who presents this as the first of his adventures.
recaps.in_short: Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III is the small, thoughtful and thoroughly unimpressive son of Stoick the Vast, chief of the Hairy Hooligan tribe on the island of Berk. To be initiated into the tribe, he and nine other boys must each steal a dragon from the nursery inside Wild Dragon Cliff and train it in time for the Thor'sday Thursday festival, on pain of exile. Hiccup ends up with the worst dragon of the lot, a tiny, toothless and utterly disobedient Common or Garden dragon he names Toothless. The tribe's training manual advises only that a boy should yell at his dragon, so Hiccup falls back on a secret of his own: he can speak Dragonese. Toothless disgraces him at the festival anyway and Hiccup is exiled, until two enormous sea dragons wash up on Berk and the only person who can do anything about them is the boy who can talk to dragons. He destroys the monster, is welcomed back, and is recognised at last as a hero of an unexpected kind.

recaps.text: On the island of Berk, ten boys of the Hairy Hooligan tribe are put through the initiation programme run by Gobber the Belch. To pass, each boy must steal a sleeping dragon from the nursery inside Wild Dragon Cliff, train it, and present it at the Thor'sday Thursday festival; anyone who fails is exiled from the tribe. Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III, the small and unimpressive son of the chief, Stoick the Vast, is not expected to manage any of it, and his cousin Snotlout says so at length. The raid goes wrong when the sleeping dragons wake and the boys have to run for the cliff top, but every boy comes away with a dragon. Snotlout has a splendid Monstrous Nightmare called Fireworm. Hiccup ends up with the least impressive dragon on the island, an ordinary Common or Garden dragon with no teeth, which he names Toothless.

Training begins from the tribe's only manual, a book by Professor Yobbish whose entire advice is that you should yell at the dragon. Yelling works well enough for the other boys, but not for Toothless, who is greedy, idle and contrary, refuses to hunt, tells obvious lies and takes offence at everything. Hiccup has an advantage he keeps to himself: he has quietly taught himself Dragonese by listening to dragons, so instead of shouting he argues, bargains and pleads with Toothless in the dragon's own language. He tells nobody, since talking to dragons is not a thing Hooligans respect. His grandfather, Old Wrinkly, is the one adult who suspects the boy might have a use for it, and hints that heroism comes in more than one shape. With Thor'sday Thursday approaching, Toothless is still doing exactly as he pleases.

Thor'sday Thursday arrives and the boys must show their dragons obeying them in front of the whole tribe. Hiccup's careful Dragonese counts for nothing when Toothless picks a fight over food, the dragons turn on one another and the ceremony collapses into a riot. Hiccup and Fishlegs are judged failures and exiled from the Hairy Hooligans, to Stoick's public shame and Snotlout's satisfaction.

Two colossal sea dragons, the Green Death and the Purple Death, are washed up on the shore at Berk, each of them big enough to eat the entire tribe, and Viking weapons are useless against them. Hiccup, exiled and with nothing left to lose, is the only person able to speak to them. He goads the two monsters into fighting each other, and while they are occupied he sends Toothless and Fishlegs's dragon Horrorcow into the surviving dragon's nostrils to set it alight from within, so that the gas it makes its own fire with destroys it. Hiccup is thrown into the sea and nearly drowns; Toothless drags him out. Berk is saved, the exile is cancelled, and Hiccup is honoured as a hero by the tribe that had written him off, with Stoick openly proud of his son for the first time. Toothless remains precisely as disobedient as before.

characters.description: The small, thoughtful heir of the Hairy Hooligans, now well used to being the least Viking-like boy in his tribe. Hiccup can speak Dragonese, a rare skill he still keeps quiet, and usually survives by noticing what louder heroes miss.
characters.name: Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III

characters.description: Hiccup's tiny Common or Garden dragon. Toothless is greedy, vain and disobedient, but he and Hiccup have faced enough danger together to make them a real team, even when Toothless insists otherwise.
characters.name: Toothless

characters.description: Hiccup's loyal friend: short-sighted, nervous, allergic to reptiles and no more suited to ordinary Viking heroics than Hiccup is.
characters.name: Fishlegs

characters.description: A fearless Bog-Burglar girl and Hiccup's friend. Camicazi is a gifted thief and lock-picker who treats danger as an invitation rather than a warning.
characters.name: Camicazi

characters.description: Chief of the Hairy Hooligans and Hiccup's father, a huge, noisy believer in the direct approach to any problem.
characters.name: Stoick the Vast

characters.description: The Hooligan boys' enormous teacher, whose lessons favour shouting, weapons and dangerous practical exercises.
characters.name: Gobber the Belch

characters.description: Hiccup's strong, boastful cousin and rival, who remains certain that he would make a much better future chief.
characters.name: Snotface Snotlout

characters.description: A celebrated wandering hero with the size, confidence and fighting skill that Viking stories promise. His sudden arrival gives Hiccup a protector who seems able to handle any ordinary danger.
characters.name: Humungously Hotshot

characters.description: The fierce daughter of UG the Uglithug. Tantrum has an old and very personal reason to be angry with Humungously Hotshot.
characters.name: Tantrum O'Ugerly

characters.description: Chief of the Uglithugs and Tantrum's father, an imposing Viking with little patience for the man who once disappointed his daughter.
characters.name: UG the Uglithug

characters.description: A deadly breed of fire dragon associated with the volcanic danger threatening the islands. Exterminators are built to survive heat that would kill a human.
characters.name: Exterminator Dragons

recaps.ending: Hiccup's warnings prove justified: the volcanic crisis is real, and the fire dragons turn the islands into a place where strength alone is no protection. Hiccup, Toothless, Fishlegs and Camicazi survive the eruption, and Hiccup's ability to understand dragons helps him find a way through a disaster that the adults cannot simply fight. Humungously Hotshot also faces the promise he abandoned years before. He returns to Tantrum O'Ugerly instead of running from his past again, and the two are reconciled. Berk and its people survive, although the adventure leaves more evidence that Hiccup's quiet sort of heroism is the kind the archipelago actually needs. He remains Stoick's unlikely heir, with Toothless beside him and with most of the tribe still unaware of how important his Dragonese has become.
recaps.in_short: During a dangerously hot season, Hiccup discovers that fire dragons and the volcanoes beneath the Viking islands are becoming a threat. The famous hero Humungously Hotshot appears and is given the job of guarding him, seeming to be everything a Viking champion should be. Hiccup, Fishlegs and Camicazi learn that the danger is larger than a few dragon attacks: an eruption could destroy whole communities. Their efforts bring them into conflict with Exterminator dragons and carry them into the volcanic disaster itself. Hiccup survives by understanding the dragons and thinking past the obvious answers. Humungous, meanwhile, has to face Tantrum O'Ugerly, the woman he left behind years ago. The islands survive the eruption, and Humungous finally returns to Tantrum rather than fleeing his old promise again.

recaps.text: Previously: Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III, the undersized heir of the Hairy Hooligans, has repeatedly saved people who expected very little from him. He has a tiny and disobedient dragon called Toothless and a secret gift for speaking Dragonese. His closest friends are the anxious Fishlegs and Camicazi, a fearless young Bog-Burglar. Hiccup has survived Roman captivity, the treachery of Alvin, and a winter voyage to steal the only potato that could cure Fishlegs of Vorpentitis. That last journey made an enemy of Norbert the Nutjob. Hiccup is still a poor fighter by Viking standards, but experience has shown that patience, languages and careful plans can do what axes cannot.

An unusually fierce hot season has made ordinary Viking training more dangerous than ever. Hiccup encounters signs that the heat is not merely bad weather: fire dragons are moving, and creatures able to live around volcanoes are appearing where they should not. His warnings receive the usual doubtful response. The arrival of Humungously Hotshot changes the balance. Humungous is a famous hero of exactly the sort Hiccup is always told to become, and his strength makes him an impressive protector. Even so, Hiccup remains troubled by the pattern behind the dragon attacks and begins looking for the danger that everyone else is missing.

Hiccup, Fishlegs and Camicazi follow the evidence toward the volcanic islands. Exterminator dragons make the journey deadly, but the larger threat is the land itself: pressure and heat are building toward an eruption. Humungously Hotshot can defeat enemies in a fight, yet his past catches up with him when the group meets the Uglithugs. Their chief, UG, has not forgotten him, and neither has UG's daughter Tantrum O'Ugerly. Humungous once left Tantrum waiting for him, so the great hero's unfinished promise becomes part of the present crisis.

The volcano begins to turn Hiccup's warnings into fact. Fire dragons, smoke and molten rock leave no safe route that can be won by force. Hiccup has to rely on Dragonese, Toothless and the help of his friends while the adults struggle to protect their tribes. Humungous is forced to choose whether to keep behaving like a wandering legend or accept responsibility for the people he left behind. The group presses on through the eruption because escaping for themselves is not enough; the islands and everyone living on them remain in danger.

Hiccup, Toothless, Fishlegs and Camicazi make it through the volcanic disaster and help prevent the fire dragons and eruption from destroying the island communities. The solution depends less on fighting than on Hiccup's willingness to understand the creatures around him and act while the larger Vikings are still arguing. Humungously Hotshot also stops running from his own unfinished story. He faces Tantrum O'Ugerly, makes peace with her and returns to the future he abandoned. Berk survives, and Hiccup comes home still small and still unlike the conventional hero his tribe imagines, but once again responsible for saving people who underestimated him.

characters.description: The older Schlegel sister, an intelligent and composed woman living in London on a comfortable inheritance. She values art, discussion, friendship, and personal connection, but also has the practical judgment that her more impulsive sister sometimes lacks. Her curiosity about the Wilcoxes gradually draws her into a family whose outlook is very different from her own.
characters.name: Margaret Schlegel

characters.description: Margaret's younger sister, passionate, generous, and quick to act on her feelings. While staying with the Wilcox family at Howards End, she mistakes an intense attraction to Paul for a lasting engagement, beginning the uneasy connection between the two families.
characters.name: Helen Schlegel

characters.description: The younger Wilcox son, preparing to leave England for work in Nigeria. During Helen's visit to Howards End, the two briefly believe themselves in love and announce an engagement that almost immediately collapses.
characters.name: Paul Wilcox

characters.description: The Schlegel sisters' aunt, protective of their respectability and alarmed by Helen's sudden engagement. She travels to Howards End intending to investigate and becomes entangled in an embarrassing misunderstanding before the families have properly met.
characters.name: Aunt Juley Munt

characters.description: The practical, prosperous head of the Wilcox family, whose business interests and faith in property, work, and imperial commerce leave little room for the Schlegels' abstract ideals. He is confident in public affairs and accustomed to having his judgments accepted.
characters.name: Henry Wilcox

characters.description: Henry and Ruth Wilcox's elder son, energetic, conventional, and fiercely protective of the family's interests. He distrusts the Schlegels and interprets challenges to his father's authority as attacks on the family itself.
characters.name: Charles Wilcox

characters.description: Henry Wilcox's quiet first wife and the person most deeply attached to Howards End, the country house she inherited through her own family. Her calm manner and intuitive sense of place fascinate Margaret, with whom she forms an unexpected friendship.
characters.name: Ruth Wilcox

characters.description: Henry and Ruth's daughter, a cheerful young woman immersed in the Wilcoxes' active social world. She shares her family's assumptions and later becomes the occasion for a large country wedding.
characters.name: Evie Wilcox

characters.description: A poorly paid insurance clerk who attends a Beethoven concert near the Schlegels. Earnest and self-conscious, he pursues books and music as a path toward a richer life, despite having little money or leisure and feeling out of place among the comfortably educated.
characters.name: Leonard Bast

characters.description: Margaret and Helen's younger brother, an Oxford student whose dry reserve contrasts with his sisters' emotional engagement with other people. He participates in the family's intellectual life but generally keeps its complications at a distance.
characters.name: Tibby Schlegel

characters.description: Leonard Bast's older companion and wife, whose loud manner and shabby appearance embarrass him. She is suspicious of his contact with the Schlegels and carries knowledge of a past that will later connect the households.
characters.name: Jacky Bast

characters.description: Charles Wilcox's wife, sociable and talkative, with a habit of repeating family information without recognizing its importance. She is firmly situated within the Wilcox circle and its conventional view of events.
characters.name: Dolly Wilcox

characters.description: An elderly local woman near Howards End who remembers the house's earlier life and treats it as a place with claims beyond legal ownership. Her unexpected recognition of Margaret strengthens the sense that Margaret belongs there.
characters.name: Miss Avery

recaps.ending: Leonard comes to Howards End intending to acknowledge his part in Helen's pregnancy. Charles, convinced that the Wilcox family must be avenged, strikes him with the flat of a sword. Leonard falls against a bookcase and dies; Charles is convicted of manslaughter and imprisoned. The shock breaks Henry's confidence, and Margaret takes charge of their life together. Fourteen months later, Margaret, Helen, Helen's young son, and Henry are living at Howards End, while Helen has chosen not to marry. Henry tells the assembled family that Margaret will receive the house for her lifetime and that it will then pass to Helen's son. The arrangement unknowingly fulfills Ruth Wilcox's discarded wish that Margaret should have Howards End. The London properties will go to Henry's children. The novel closes with the house inhabited by the Schlegel sisters and the next generation, while the surrounding countryside remains threatened by London's expansion.
recaps.in_short: The cultured Schlegel sisters become entangled with the wealthy, practical Wilcox family and with Leonard Bast, a poor clerk seeking intellectual improvement. Margaret befriends the dying Ruth Wilcox, who privately leaves her Howards End, but Ruth's family suppresses the informal bequest. Margaret later marries Henry Wilcox. His careless financial advice ruins Leonard, and his past affair with Leonard's wife exposes the limits of his moral certainty. Helen, trying to help Leonard, becomes pregnant by him and retreats abroad. When she returns, Margaret insists that she be sheltered at Howards End, breaking with Henry over his hypocrisy. Leonard is killed when Henry's son Charles attacks him and is imprisoned for manslaughter. Henry collapses, and Margaret becomes the household's directing force. She, Helen, Helen's son, and Henry settle at Howards End; Henry arranges for Margaret to inherit it and for the house eventually to pass to Helen's child, fulfilling Ruth's original intention.

recaps.text: While visiting the Wilcox family at their country house, Howards End, the impulsive Helen Schlegel announces that she is engaged to Paul Wilcox. Her older sister Margaret tries to respond calmly, but their alarmed aunt travels to the house and mistakes Paul's brother Charles for the prospective bridegroom. By the time the confusion is resolved, Helen and Paul have already recognized that their attachment cannot last. The incident leaves the cultured, liberal Schlegels and the business-minded Wilcoxes embarrassed and wary of one another. Back in London, Margaret, Helen, and their brother Tibby attend a Beethoven concert. Helen accidentally leaves with Leonard Bast's umbrella, bringing the poorly paid clerk into contact with the sisters. Leonard is earnest about books and culture but painfully conscious of the social and financial gulf between them.

The Wilcoxes take a London flat near the Schlegels, and Margaret forms an unexpectedly intimate friendship with Ruth Wilcox. Ruth's deepest loyalty is to Howards End, a house inherited from her own family, while her husband and children treat property more instrumentally. Already ill, Ruth attempts a final outing with Margaret and imagines the younger woman living at the house. After Ruth dies, the Wilcoxes discover a handwritten note asking that Howards End be given to Margaret. Because the note is informal and seems irrational to them, they destroy it without telling her. Margaret knows only that her new friend has died. Meanwhile Leonard returns for his umbrella and the Schlegels meet Jacky, the woman with whom he lives. Their wish to help him is sincere, but it is shaped by assumptions that their money protects them from having to examine.

The Schlegels learn that the lease on their London home will not be renewed, making questions of houses and belonging increasingly urgent. Leonard Bast continues his effort to educate himself while supporting Jacky on a small salary. When Margaret encounters Henry Wilcox again, she asks his professional opinion of Leonard's employer. Henry warns that the insurance company is unsafe. The sisters pass this advice to Leonard, who leaves his secure post, only for the company to survive while his new employer later dismisses him. The Wilcoxes move through houses and business decisions with confidence, whereas Leonard has no cushion against one mistaken recommendation. Margaret grows to respect Henry's energy and competence even as she sees his limitations. Their renewed acquaintance begins to bind the families more closely than either side expected.

Henry asks Margaret to marry him, and she accepts, believing affection and patience can connect his practical world with her own values. Helen distrusts the match, especially after Leonard loses his job as an indirect result of Henry's advice. At Evie Wilcox's wedding in Shropshire, Helen arrives with Leonard and Jacky, intending to confront the Wilcoxes with the consequences of their carelessness. Jacky drunkenly recognizes Henry and reveals that he had an affair with her years earlier, when she was young and he was married to Ruth. Henry expects Margaret to end the engagement, but she distinguishes his past failure from his present self and forgives him. Her response gives him relief without yet forcing him to apply the same generosity to anyone else. Leonard and Jacky remain in severe poverty, and Helen is distressed by how little the confrontation has repaired.

Margaret marries Henry and tries to make a humane life within the restless Wilcox household. Helen leaves England, avoids her family, and communicates only indirectly. When illness in the family brings her back, Margaret realizes that Helen is pregnant and arranges for the sisters to spend one night together at Howards End. Henry refuses to let Helen stay there because her pregnancy is outside marriage. Margaret confronts him with his willingness to excuse his own affair while condemning Helen, and she decides to leave him. The house itself becomes a refuge: Miss Avery, an elderly local woman who remembers its history, has unpacked the Schlegels' stored possessions there as though anticipating their arrival. Leonard, burdened by poverty and by his connection to Helen, is drawn toward the same reckoning.

Leonard comes to Howards End to face what has happened. Charles Wilcox, acting on his belief that the family's honor has been violated, attacks him with the flat of a sword. Leonard falls against a bookcase and dies; his poor health contributes to the fatal result. Charles is convicted of manslaughter and sent to prison. The disaster shatters Henry's certainty, and Margaret returns, now effectively directing their shared life. Fourteen months later, Margaret and Henry live at Howards End with Helen and Helen's young son. Helen remains unmarried but has recovered a sense of peace. Henry announces that Margaret is to have Howards End for life and that it will afterward pass to Helen's boy, while his other property goes to his children. Neither he nor Margaret knows that this outcome fulfills Ruth's destroyed note. The house finally becomes a settled home linking the families and generations, even as London continues to advance into the countryside.
